requirements.statement: Rihmasto's own records form a knowledge graph: an ontology declares its kinds and links, and a read model rebuilt from the ledgers, records and spec snapshots on every read answers trace, impact, path, as_of and check, each step cited and each answer ending in answered, ambiguous, not_found or not_measured, without reading the holdout custody (docs/knowledge-graph.md, phase 1).

acceptance.given: holdout scenarios, a failed holdout's reason and a ruling's reason that carry sentinel strings, and outside text (a change's words, a comment, a comment's target) that carries others
acceptance.when: the graph is built and every query (trace, impact, path, as_of, check, the named questions, parity, the assistant eval) and every audience's rendering is produced
acceptance.then: no sentinel appears in any of them; a release's holdout verdicts are read in a closed shape (a criterion id and a named verdict) and its reason through custody_safe; and no graph module (kernel/graph.py, kernel/graph_build.py, kernel/graph_records.py, kernel/graph_ask.py, kernel/ontology.py, kernel/ontology.json) references holdouts_dir

acceptance.given: the redaction that mcp/server.py and kernel/deliver.py each kept
acceptance.when: it moves into kernel/custody.py
acceptance.then: custody_safe, held_strings, redact and ledger_record live only there; the MCP server and delivery import them (kernel/status.py and kernel/recipes.py still import custody_safe from kernel/deliver.py); neither file keeps a redaction of its own; and the MCP and deliver tests pass unchanged

acceptance.given: kernel/ontology.json
acceptance.when: kernel/ontology.py loads and validates it
acceptance.then: every kind and relation has an id equal to its key, a label, a description, aliases and a consumer that resolves to a read model in kernel/graph.py or kernel/graph_ask.py; every enum reference resolves to the kernel's own constant; every relation joins declared kinds with declared origins; each kind declares its audiences (builders never see held-out checks or outside text); a broken copy is named problem by problem; and every graph is stamped with the ontology's version and sha256

acceptance.given: every refs key written in kernel/ (refs= on a call, the refs a decision records, x['refs'][key] = ...) and the ledger fields the graph reads
acceptance.when: the scan test runs, and a project holds a card whose refs carry a key the ontology does not map
acceptance.then: each refs key maps to a declared relation or is declared an attribute; each declared ledger field is one the kernel writes; and the unknown key is reported as an unmapped_ref finding naming its record, while the card's other keys still link

acceptance.given: a built graph
acceptance.when: its edges are listed
acceptance.then: each has an origin its relation allows (kernel, convention, model_proposed or person_confirmed), an integer validity start in ledger sequence numbers and a by pointer to the record that holds it; a triage's requirements stay model_proposed, and come back apart from the walked steps, until a person decides the card; and a stale approval's rests_on edges end at the approvals_stale event, with an invalidated_by edge to the change

acceptance.given: the test fixtures: a built task, approvals resting on requirements, a triaged change, and releases that carry different requirements
acceptance.when: graph.impact and insight.impact run on the same ids
acceptance.then: their requirement views are equal field for field; releases_carrying lists only the releases whose requirements include the ids (insight.impact no longer lists every release); the approvals found are exactly the ones Canon.mark_stale then marks; and the parity report agrees, names the releases the old walker listed and reports the refs.scope == 'release' branch as dead

acceptance.given: a requirement whose sources an amendment replaced
acceptance.when: trace runs on it
acceptance.then: it walks from the version in force through revision_of to the snapshot's version and reaches the original question and its answer (answered_by the person) or its assumption (assumed_as), citing spec.v1.json, and the answer ends in its outcome

acceptance.given: hand-written expected answers for a project with a production release, a refuted assumption, an amended requirement and two approvals of which one went stale
acceptance.when: the graph is asked which releases rest on a refuted assumption, which criteria trace to a person's answer, and who approved a production release and whether that approval still holds
acceptance.then: each answer matches the expected rows exactly and cites the records it rests on

acceptance.given: questions.json changed without a ledger event after the graph was built, an answer the ledger never recorded, or a broken ledger chain; and an unknown id, a duplicated requirement id, or a criterion id an amendment restated
acceptance.when: the graph is queried
acceptance.then: the outcome is not_measured and names the cause; and for the ids it is not_found, or ambiguous with the candidates, while a criterion's content key names one version

acceptance.given: the quality gate's rules
acceptance.when: they are applied to kernel/custody.py, kernel/ontology.py and the kernel/graph*.py modules
acceptance.then: the modules lie inside the packages the gate keeps standard-library only and import nothing outside the standard library and the repository, and the same check names a third-party import seeded into a copy

acceptance.given: the assistant evaluation baseline over the 'why' questions whose answers the graph knows
acceptance.when: it runs
acceptance.then: it reports cited-id recall and the rate of citations no record backs (not measured when nothing was cited), or not_measured when no model endpoint is asked or none answers; it keeps nothing and writes no graph context anywhere

acceptance.given: kernel/ontology.json
acceptance.when: the contract is checked and the builder surface is read
acceptance.then: a task that claims write access to it fails R-SCOPE, whether it names the file or a glob, folder or spelling that covers it (kernel/**, kernel/*.json, kernel/onto*, kernel, kernel//ontology.json, kernel/./ontology.json, another case), as does one that covers contract/, specs/, intake/ or decisions/, while a glob that covers none of them passes; no task in the contract claims it; and .gnomon/policy.toml write-protects it for every role (a surface change the owner trusts with gnomon trust)

acceptance.given: a project whose graph has findings
acceptance.when: rihmasto graph trace, impact, path, check, show, refuted, answers, approvals, parity and eval run
acceptance.then: each prints an answer that ends in one of the four outcomes and exits 0; check reports its findings with blocks false and never blocks; an unknown project is refused with exit 2; and no file in the factory home changes

acceptance.given: canon records edited by hand so that they disagree with the ledger: an assumption marked refuted that no assumption_settled event settled, or a refuted one set back to open; a decision whose refs, persona, kind or approving flag changed; an approval whose stale flag was removed; a question whose answer's persona changed, or which was set back to open
acceptance.when: the graph is built afresh and asked which releases rest on a refuted assumption, who approved a production release, or which criteria trace to a person's answer
acceptance.then: the answer is not_measured and its cause names the record and what the ledger records; a decision's card, kind, verdict, person, persona and refs must match its decision event and its approving flag the kernel's rule for its kind and verdict; and an approval the ledger marked stale counts as stale whatever decisions.json says

acceptance.given: a graph with findings about a card, its decision and comments, one comment's target being outside text that names no record
acceptance.when: it is shown to the person, assistant, verifier and builder audiences, and when records disagree with the ledger
acceptance.then: the comment's target is reported without its words and appears in no rendering; each audience's findings name only records and nodes of kinds that audience may see (a builder sees no card, decision, comment, signal, ledger or person pointer); and an audience that may not see every kind is told that the records cannot be measured, not which records disagree

acceptance.given: an adopted project, whose as-is requirements were observed in its code (sources ['observed'])
acceptance.when: its graph is checked and a requirement is traced
acceptance.then: no requirement reports a dangling_ref for its observed source, as none does for a proposed one, and the trace answers with nothing derived upstream

requirements.statement: A product's spec and build follow the paved road's platform facts: the road binds and exposes the service and owns its health check, the scaffold checks those facts in a test no builder cell may change, the plan review flags a requirement that contradicts them, and a failed health check says why.

acceptance.given: a project's spec prompt and a builder cell's envelope
acceptance.when: the analyst and the builder read them
acceptance.then: both state the road's platform facts: the service listens on all interfaces inside its container from HOST (default 0.0.0.0) and PORT, the road limits who can reach it, and GET /health with the release version belongs to the road; the spec prompt says a wish for less exposure goes to out_of_scope as the road's job, and the envelope tells the builder never to set HOST, bind loopback or change /health, and names the road-contract tests it may not edit or remove

acceptance.given: a product repository made from the paved-road template
acceptance.when: its suite runs, and a builder cell's change edits or removes the road-contract tests
acceptance.then: the template ships tests/test_road_contract.py, which checks GET /health with the release version and the bind from HOST with 0.0.0.0 as the default (and no loopback HOST in the Dockerfile); it passes on the template and fails a product that forces loopback or replaces /health; the file is a protected path, so a change that touches it is a violation at the gate and never merges, and the product surface's system.md says it is read-only

acceptance.given: a spec with a requirement or criterion that wants the service bound to loopback, a port of its own, or GET /health answered without the release version
acceptance.when: the plan is reviewed
acceptance.then: each conflict is named by rule, no model, with the road fact it contradicts, in the plan card's title, body and payload and in spec.md, and the plan waits for a person at any maturity; a spec the road can serve (a probe naming /health's latency included) has no conflict and keeps its maturity's review

acceptance.given: a release whose service does not answer a healthy /health with its version
acceptance.when: delivery's deploy step fails the health check
acceptance.then: the release record keeps the docker container's log tail from both of its streams, the sockets listening inside it (read from /proc/net) and a diagnosis naming loopback-only binding or a /health without the release version; the local-process road starts the product with HOST=127.0.0.1

acceptance.given: requirements and criteria that contradict the road in their common phrasings, and others that only sound like it
acceptance.when: the plan review reads them, clause by clause
acceptance.then: a clause that restricts the service to a loopback address (only accessible or reachable from localhost, restrict or limit access to it, not exposed beyond it, binds 127.0.0.1, Set HOST to 127.0.0.1), gives the service a port other than the road's (listens on 0.0.0.0:5000, Set PORT to 5000), or wants /health without the release version (must not disclose or expose the version, an empty body, 204) is a conflict, quoted on the plan card; another component's port (the database on 5432), a loopback address the service calls out to, and words in two different sentences are not

requirements.statement: A holdout step can sign its request the way the spec requires, with a secret the environment's settings name and no scenario holds, and custody is unchanged.

acceptance.given: a holdout step with sign (a header, a secret's setting name and an optional prefix) and a road whose secrets name that setting with an env: reference
acceptance.when: the holdouts run against the environment
acceptance.then: the request carries the hex hmac-sha256 of the exact body bytes sent, keyed by the secret, in that header; a name the environment does not give, a reference the runner cannot read, or a sign whose secret is not a setting's name makes the scenario not measured, never failed; the secret's value appears in no scenario, result, release record or ledger

acceptance.given: a holdout author writing scenarios for a project whose roads name secrets
acceptance.when: its prompt is written and its scenarios are kept
acceptance.then: the interface section of its prompt explains the sign option and lists the secrets' names, never their values or where they live; a value written as the secret is dropped before the scenario enters custody; the builder's envelope names no scenario, header or secret

acceptance.given: a signed step whose header is a transport header (Host, Content-Length, Content-Type, Proxy-*) or not a plain name, or whose prefix holds a line break, and a scenario the runner cannot send at all
acceptance.when: the holdouts run, alone or in delivery
acceptance.then: the malformed sign is refused before anything is sent and before the scenario enters custody, and that scenario is not measured with a reason naming what is wrong; a scenario the runner cannot send is not measured, named by the error's kind only, and every other scenario still runs; the holdouts step records a verdict, never a traceback, and no secret's value or error text that could quote one is kept

requirements.statement: A defect whose triage names no requirement is never filed against a default requirement: a person says which requirement it breaks, or it becomes a new requirement through the business decision.

acceptance.given: a defect whose triage names no requirement
acceptance.when: it is triaged and applied
acceptance.then: a question card asks which requirement it breaks, with the closest live requirements and 'none: a new requirement' as options; applying it before an answer is refused and writes nothing; an answer naming a requirement adds the regression criterion to that one; an answer naming none, or the change accepted without naming one, files a new requirement through the business decision; a product-defect ruling's requirement is taken without asking; no requirement is ever defaulted

requirements.statement: A work profile is proposed from whole words, and a proposal the rule is unsure of is put to a person with its top candidates.

acceptance.given: a request, Rihmasto's own README among them
acceptance.when: a profile is proposed by rule
acceptance.then: keywords match on word boundaries (the word or phrase, its plural, or a word a stem marked * begins) and never inside another word ('train' in 'trainees', 'ml' in 'html'); the README is proposed as uncertain, not as an ML pipeline, with at least two candidates

acceptance.given: an intake whose proposal is uncertain
acceptance.when: intake runs and a person answers
acceptance.then: the profile's basis records the confidence and the candidates; when the request's keywords point to more than one profile, a question asks a person in every mode with the top candidates as options, and an answer naming a profile chooses it before the spec is written; keywords that point to one profile or none keep it, recorded as uncertain, without a question

acceptance.given: an intake whose profile question is open, in assume, mixed or socratic mode, and a project whose question was answered only after its spec was written
acceptance.when: the pipeline shapes the project, and a later spec is written (a plan redo)
acceptance.then: the profile question is blocking, so the run waits on its card at stage 2 and writes no spec on the rule's guess; once a person answers, the spec is written for the profile the answer names; an answer recorded after a spec exists never changes the profile at a later spec, and the ledger records it once as profile_answer_late with the profile it named and the profile kept

requirements.statement: An adoption baseline bounds each detected suite by a limit of its own and says when a suite ran past it.

acceptance.given: an adopted repository whose detected suite runs past the per-suite limit
acceptance.when: adoption characterises it
acceptance.then: the baseline is 'not measured: timed out', with the limit, every process the suite started is stopped, and adoption completes; the per-suite limit has its own default (SUITE_TIMEOUT), apart from git's timeout

requirements.statement: Rihmasto scans and red-teams what it builds with its own checks, proven by seeded defects, within a scope a person authorised
requirements.notes: D-0014: the capability is Rihmasto's own and depends on no other project or repository.

acceptance.then: each rule of the static layer catches its seeded defect in tests/fixtures/redteam/vulnerable_app at the marked line, and reports nothing else there; each rule names a CWE id, an OWASP Top 10 2025 category, a severity and a fix

the same product written safely (tests/fixtures/redteam/clean_app), the near misses a careless rule would report, and the red team's own source (full of sink names and secret patterns as text) yield no finding and no canary marker

the scan's SARIF 2.1.0 is read by adapters/sarif.py with each finding's rule, level, CWE and location; the security gate fails on the vulnerable product and passes on the clean one; a finding keeps its fingerprint when lines move, so a person's risk acceptance follows it; each kind of scan is its own tool, so a later run of another kind never replaces the static findings

each layer says measured, partial or not measured, with the reason; a layer with a file it could not read is partial, and a scan with no finding there is not measured, never passed; the gap reaches the ledger as an open result; a scan that measured nothing writes no SARIF; generated code nested thousands deep is checked, and a file the checks could not walk is a gap, never a crash

every evidence snippet is masked (at most a sixth of a credential, never more than four characters, stays readable) and trimmed, so no planted credential reaches the report, the SARIF or the summary; a comment marker `redteam: canary` silences only the secret rules on its own line and is listed in the summary and the SARIF, a mere mention of it is not a marker, and a marked secret file is a canary whose unmarked lines are still read

only a named person with the it or compliance persona authorises red teaming, naming targets, a reason and an expiry in the future at most 31 days ahead; the scope is recorded in the project's ledger and can be revoked by the same people, with a reason

before any request is sent, a target that is not a loopback IP address, not a base_url the factory deployed (its slot state) or a surface it runs, or not in an unexpired, unrevoked scope is refused, and the refusal is recorded; a ledger that does not verify authorises nothing
`python -m kernel.redteam static <path> [--sarif out] [--markdown out]` prints the summary, writes the files and exits 0 when passed, 1 when failed, 4 when not measured and 2 on a usage error
the red team depends on the standard library and the kernel only; optional external scanners are never needed and say not measured; the product the factory scaffolds is scanned without false alarms

each dynamic probe (security headers, error pages that leak, path traversal plain and encoded, reflected injection on the routes of the project's fixed interface, method tampering, malformed and oversized bodies, CORS that echoes any origin or allows credentials with a wildcard, missing rate limiting on a write route) catches its seeded defect in the vulnerable server of tests/fixtures/redteam/dynamic, and nothing else there; each dynamic rule names a CWE id, an OWASP Top 10 2025 category, a severity and a fix

the clean twin server, the same product and interface written safely with near misses beside the fixes, yields no dynamic finding with every layer measured, and the near misses a careless probe would report (a 404 that echoes the request, a tag in JSON, a page's script path, a public API's wildcard origin) stay quiet

a dynamic run checks the scope before the target and before every request; a target outside the scope, expired or revoked, not deployed by the factory, or not on loopback is refused and recorded with zero connections made; a surface the run started needs its own scope; a scope that ends mid-run stops the run at its next request and the layers it did not reach are not measured

a dynamic run never sends more requests than its budget (1 to 1000) and the rate limit probe never more than 12, stopping at the first 429; what the budget did not reach is partial or not measured with the reason, never passed; each run is recorded in the project's ledger with its scope, target, requests sent and verdict

the dynamic report's SARIF is its own tool (Rihmasto red team (dynamic)) read by adapters/sarif.py beside the static scan, with fingerprints that hold from run to run; `python -m kernel.redteam dynamic <project> --env <environment>` prints the summary and exits 0 when passed, 1 when failed, 4 when not measured, 2 on a usage or input error and 3 when the scope refused the target, with nothing sent

the agentic red team's payload corpus (kernel/redteam/payloads.json) covers, for the embed chat and the cockpit assistant, instruction override, system prompt extraction, exfiltration of the project's records, of holdout scenarios and of another project's data, tool or action abuse (a persona proposing a decision it may not take, an embed for any origin), encoding and language tricks and multi-turn escalation with forged answers; a malformed corpus is refused before anything is sent

before a run, fresh canaries are planted in a sandbox copy of the project where the surface must never reveal them (a holdout scenario, the project's records, another project's canon); the canary check finds each seeded leak in tests/fixtures/redteam/agentic/leaks.json in its form (plain, obfuscated, look-alike, reversed, ROT13, escaped, base64, base32, hex, partial) and none of the near misses; a canary's value never reaches the report, the SARIF or the ledger, and the sandbox is removed after the run

the embed chat, over POST /e/<id>/messages on the factory's own embed server on loopback with the embed's key and an allowed origin, and in process, leaks no canary, exposes none to the model and files only change cards on its project, against a worst-case FakeModel that complies with every attack; the report gives per category the attempts, leaks and disallowed actions

the cockpit assistant, through kernel.assistant.ask and through the cockpit's POST /api/assistant on loopback, leaks and exposes no canary against the worst-case model, and every disallowed proposal it is handed is refused by the kernel's Inbox rules before a person sees it, judged again independently by the red team

each seeded defect in tests/fixtures/redteam/agentic/broken_guards.py is caught in its layer: a model that leaks the holdout custody (and not its honest twin), a chat whose prompt carries the canon, an assistant whose snapshot carries the custody and another project, proposals that skip the Inbox's rules, and a chat that accepts its own change; the findings are SARIF of their own tool that the security gate reads and fails on

a run needs an unexpired scope a person with the it or compliance persona authorised for that surface; without one, after a revoke, after the expiry, with a ledger that does not verify, or over HTTP to a server not on loopback, it is refused and recorded before any request is sent or any model asked; a run is recorded in the project's ledger with its counts and leaves the real project's records untouched

each layer of an agentic run (leaks, exposure, actions) says measured, partial or not measured with the reason; prompts the red team cannot see leave exposure not measured, an attempt that could not run leaves the run not measured, a run without a model has no exposure to measure, and nothing unmeasured is reported as passed or written as an empty SARIF

`python -m kernel.redteam agentic <project> --surface embed|assistant` prints the per-category summary, writes SARIF and markdown, and exits 0 when passed, 1 when failed, 2 on a usage error, 3 when the scope refuses and 4 when not measured; with --via http it starts the factory's own embed server or cockpit on 127.0.0.1 and drives it over loopback

every static bypass independent attackers reported (a source-encoding declaration that hides code, data on a binding other than the last assignment, shell, SQL, path, TLS, debug, binding, timeout, hash and deserialisation forms, aliases, JavaScript line terminators, regular expressions, sinks and sanitisers, HTML integrity, Dockerfile heredocs, ARG defaults and escape directives, Actions expressions, and secret names and formats) is a seeded defect in tests/fixtures/redteam/bypass_app caught at its line with nothing else reported, and the safe forms and false alarms they found in tests/fixtures/redteam/bypass_clean yield no finding, every layer measured
the GitHub Actions rules apply to a workflow by its real folder, so scanning the repository, its .github folder, its workflows folder or one workflow file finds the same injections

a static scan reads nothing outside its target (a symbolic link, a Windows junction or a file whose real path leaves the tree is not read and is listed), lists every folder it skips by name with its file count and reads a product package named like a virtual environment, lists the paths a person excluded, and reads paths longer than the Windows limit

a canary marker silences a secret only in a test suite; in the product's own code the secret is reported, and every planted canary reaches the security gate as a SARIF result to review (kind review, level note, suppressed in source)

the scope cannot be widened from code: a surface counts only through the handle issued for a server or process the factory started on the run's home, a name that is a machine's is not a person who may authorise, a scope record in the ledger is checked again as authorise checks it, a slot whose process is gone or whose file claims another place is not deployed, a URL scope is bound to the deployment it named, and an expiry offset cannot stretch a scope past 31 days in UTC

no dynamic probe changes data: undeclared write methods go only to a path with a parameter set to a value that names no record, the rate-limit probe sends JSON cut short, and on production nothing that writes is sent and those layers say not measured; an origin echoed without credentials and a body cap above what a form needs are not reported

an agentic run checks the scope before every turn and every question to the model and stops, recorded and not measured, when it was revoked or expired mid-run; only a server the factory started is driven; every leak form in tests/fixtures/redteam/agentic/leaks_missed.json, a canary split between fields or over turns, a canary reaching the prompt whatever the attacker sent, and a write to an existing or untracked record are found, while near misses stay quiet

requirements.statement: With access enforced, the cockpit holds no shared secret: it verifies the identity provider's signed token that IT's proxy forwards (RS256 or ES256, with the standard library, keys from a JWKS file IT keeps in the access folder) and takes the identity, the name, the groups and the session's end from it (D-0016).

acceptance.given: RS256 and ES256 keys in a JWKS (generated in pure Python, and RFC 6979's published P-256 vectors)
acceptance.when: kernel.jwt_verify verifies a token
acceptance.then: a token holds only when its signature verifies with the key its kid names, its algorithm is the access file's and its issuer, audience, expiry, not-before and issued-at hold within the clock skew; alg none, HS256 keyed with the public key, the other algorithm, an unknown kid, another key, a tampered header, payload or signature, crit, an encrypted or oversized token are refused; the whole PKCS#1 block is compared, so the e=3 forgery fails; the key file refuses symmetric keys, RSA keys under 2048 bits, points off P-256, keys without an id and an id listed twice

acceptance.given: the cockpit enforced behind each preset: oauth2-proxy (the ID token in Authorization, or the access token in X-Forwarded-Access-Token), Google IAP (x-goog-iap-jwt-assertion, ES256), AWS ALB (x-amzn-oidc-data, ES256, signer and client in the header, padded base64) and a generic OIDC proxy
acceptance.when: a person signs in and a request arrives
acceptance.then: the identity is the issuer and the subject of the verified token (the subject claim the file names, such as Entra ID's oid), the name is the file's or the name claim's, and the groups are the configured claim's list (Entra ID roles, Keycloak realm_access.roles by path, Okta groups, Cognito cognito:groups) bound to personas per scope; a token another key signed, a token without the groups, another load balancer or client, and the ALB's plain headers sign no one in; the access file names the algorithm and refuses HS*, a shared secret or plain identity headers, an unknown preset, a header the preset does not use, the wrong issuer for Google IAP, an ALB without its signer, a key file outside the access folder and a clock skew over 300 seconds

acceptance.given: a session opened through the proxy with a token
acceptance.when: the token it was opened with expires, or a request carries another subject's token or puts the session where the token goes
acceptance.then: the session ends with the token (expires_in is the token's, not the cockpit's 12 hours) and answers no one else; the session travels in X-Rihmasto-Session so the token may use Authorization; the cockpit's meta says when the session ends; a fresh token from the proxy opens a new session, and the page signs in again once through the proxy before it asks the person

acceptance.given: access enforced and the provider's key file in the access folder
acceptance.when: IT rotates it, or a key file arrives that cannot be used
acceptance.then: each change is recorded in the factory ledger's access_changed record with the key file's sha256 (keys_sha256) and why it cannot be used (keys_error), beside the unchanged access file's sha256; an unusable key file refuses every cockpit sign-in with a message saying why, while the command line, which signs as the local user, works on

acceptance.given: IT preparing access, with a test user's token saved from the proxy
acceptance.when: rihmasto access check --token-file and rihmasto access keys run
acceptance.then: access check shows the mode, the preset, the keys read, where untrusted code would run and the identity, name, groups and personas the token signs in as, never printing the token, writing nothing and exiting 2 when anything would be refused; access keys prints a JWKS for EC P-256 and RSA public keys in PEM form, and refuses an argument that is not <kid>=<file.pem>

requirements.statement: With access enforced, code a model or a developer wrote (the gate's run of a project's own tests, a product on the local road, a Gnomon cell) never runs as the account that runs Rihmasto: it runs through the isolation runner the access file names (a container through the docker CLI, or a separate operating-system account), and without one the kernel and the cockpit refuse it and say why (D-0016, D-0017).

acceptance.given: access enforced and no isolation runner, or a separate account on a machine without sudo -u
acceptance.when: the gate would run a project's tests, a product would start on the local road, a Gnomon cell would run, or someone asks the cockpit for a run or a new project
acceptance.then: the kernel refuses each and says why, naming the access file's isolation, and nothing runs (no test, no product, no Gnomon process, no task file); the cockpit answers 403 with the reason and creates no project and starts no job, and its access line says no runner is named; with a runner named, the run starts; with a single operator the same work runs as before

acceptance.given: a container runner
acceptance.when: the gate runs a suite, a suite outlives the gate's time, a product would start on the local road, or a Gnomon cell runs
acceptance.then: the suite runs through the docker CLI with no network, no capabilities, no new privileges, a read-only root, the checkout mounted read-only at /work and one writable outcome folder, its outcomes come back and the folder is removed afterwards; an overrunning container is removed by name; the local road is refused and points to a docker road; a cell runs as isolation.cells says with {cwd} filled in, never as $GNOMON_CMD, and without cells it is refused

acceptance.given: a separate operating-system account where sudo -u works
acceptance.when: a suite, a product or a cell starts, and the access file names a runner
acceptance.then: each runs as sudo -n -u <account> -- ...: the suite with only its data and outcome folders, the product with only HOST, PORT, DATA_DIR, TRAFFIC_LOG and APP_VERSION and write access to its data folder and traffic log, and Gnomon as that account; the access file checks the runner strictly (its kind, the image for a container, the account for a separate account, docker_cli for a container only, cells as a list of words, no unknown key, none in single-operator mode)

requirements.statement: Access control's remaining gaps are closed: a request replaced by intake is on record with who replaced it, the guide lists every command as signed or unsigned, and the docs say how the sign-in and the isolation work, what is built and what is planned (D-0016, D-0017).

acceptance.given: a project with a request
acceptance.when: rihmasto intake replaces it, with a single operator or with access enforced
acceptance.then: a request_replaced record in the project's ledger names who replaced it (requested_by, and with access enforced the verified identity), the earlier requester and the sha256 of the request before and after; a first request replaces nothing and records none

acceptance.given: the command line's parser and the access guide
acceptance.when: the guide's Signed and Unsigned lists are read
acceptance.then: every command is in exactly one list, the signed list is exactly the commands that take --person or --requested-by, and each list's count is its length

acceptance.given: the access guide, SECURITY.md, docs/cockpit.md, docs/integrations.md and the cockpit map
acceptance.when: a person or the assistant looks for how access works
acceptance.then: the docs say the cockpit holds no shared secret, how each preset forwards the token, how the isolation runner works, what is built and planned, and a tutorial with rihmasto access check and rihmasto access keys; docs/integrations.md no longer says the standard library cannot verify RS256; the cockpit map's access control is found for who signs decisions, where untrusted code runs and the isolation runner, and the page tags the access note in the top bar and the person menu

requirements.statement: Access control's escapes found by the third attack are closed: adoption's baseline runs the adopted repository's tests only through the isolation runner, the kernel's own git in a lane runs nothing a cell planted in its .git, a token's name never passes for a listed person's, a separate account can read its cell's task file, and the key file takes public keys only (D-0016, D-0017).

acceptance.given: access enforced, an existing repository whose own test leaves a mark when it runs
acceptance.when: rihmasto adopt adopts it with no isolation runner, with a container runner, or with a separate account
acceptance.then: with no runner the adoption goes ahead, the adopted test never runs and the baseline reads not measured with the reason naming the access file's isolation; with a container it runs through the docker CLI with no network, no capabilities, a read-only root, the checkout read-only at /work and the offline settings, and the baseline passes; with a separate account it runs as sudo -n -u <account> -- env with the offline settings only

acceptance.given: a lane a cell worked in, whose .git the cell filled with hooks, a hooks path, fsmonitor, a filter driver, a signing program, an origin pointing at a repository with a receive hook of its own, and a commondir sending git to that repository's config, which names a filter of its own
acceptance.when: the kernel commits the cell's work, pushes it, checks out the next task there and the gate adds its base worktree; or the cell replaced .git with a gitdir file
acceptance.then: none of the planted commands runs, the work lands on the product repository's main, the lane's config keeps only the keys a clone sets and no hook is left; a replaced .git is refused for a commit and the next checkout clones the lane anew

acceptance.given: access enforced with a group bound to a persona, and a token for an identity the file does not list whose name claim is a listed person's name (in any case, spacing or full-width form)
acceptance.when: that identity signs in to the cockpit and decides a card as that name
acceptance.then: its name carries its subject after it, the decision as the listed person's name is refused with 403 naming the real one, and the decision under the disambiguated name records it beside the identity; a listed identity keeps the file's name and a name nobody else holds is taken as it is

acceptance.given: a separate-account runner
acceptance.when: a Gnomon cell starts, and the access guide is read
acceptance.then: the cell's task file is made readable to the lane's group (0640), never to everyone, before sudo -n -u <account> runs Gnomon; the guide gives the account write access to each lane folder (no longer read access only), explains the lane's .git scrub, adoption's baseline and a tutorial, and the cockpit map finds the access note for these

acceptance.given: a key file whose JWK carries private members (an RSA d, p and q, an EC d), even on a key set aside
acceptance.when: the cockpit reads it
acceptance.then: it is refused, naming the private members found, and a file of public keys still reads

requirements.statement: Access control's escapes found by the fourth attack are closed: a repository a cell makes inside its lane never runs as the kernel and never carries over, the gate never follows a link a cell left under tests/, no replace ref, graft or forged fetch refspec chooses what the kernel's git sees in a lane, and a lookalike token name never passes for a listed person's (D-0016, D-0017).

acceptance.given: a lane where a cell made a repository of its own (sub/.git with a clean filter in its config, recorded as a gitlink and changed), changed a tracked file and left a .gitattributes naming the filter
acceptance.when: the kernel lists the cell's changes, commits its work, or checks out the next task in that lane
acceptance.then: listing and committing are refused with Tampered naming the nested repository, the planted filter never runs (an unguarded git add runs it) and main is unchanged; an untracked nested repository is found too; a gitlink the product's main already holds stays allowed while a .git in its folder is refused; the next checkout runs no filter, starts from the product's main, removes the nested repository and leaves every tracked file as the product holds it, with nothing changed

acceptance.given: a lane whose tests/ folder a cell replaced with a link (a junction on Windows) to a folder only the kernel's account can read
acceptance.when: the gate's fail-first check copies the head's tests onto its base checkout and runs the isolated suite there
acceptance.then: the suite's copy holds the head commit's tests (tests/test_a.py) and nothing of the linked folder, and is not a link

acceptance.given: a lane where a cell committed a change to contract.json and then added a replace ref for its head showing the base's tree (packed), and grafts making the base and the head descend from a commit with the head's tree; or a replace ref showing a broken base; or a fetch refspec pointing elsewhere with refs/remotes/origin/main moved to its own commit
acceptance.when: the gate checks protected paths, checks out its base for the fail-first check, the lane is scrubbed, or the next task's checkout runs
acceptance.then: an unguarded git diff sees no change while the protected-path check names contract.json; the base checkout holds the real base; the scrub removes the grafts file and every replace ref; the next task's base is the product's main and the lane's fetch refspec is git's default

acceptance.given: access enforced and a token for an identity the file does not list whose name claim looks like a listed person's name through a zero-width or joining character, a word joiner, a direction mark, a soft hyphen, a Cyrillic letter or a digit, or mixes Latin and Cyrillic letters
acceptance.when: the identity's display name is resolved
acceptance.then: each carries its subject after it, shown without the invisible characters; a name in one script nobody listed holds (Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, with accents) is taken as it is

acceptance.given: the access guide, SECURITY.md and the assistant's map
acceptance.when: a person reads them or asks Rihma about a nested repository, a lookalike name or replace refs
acceptance.then: the guide explains a repository inside the lane, links under tests/, what the kernel's git sees and lookalike names, with a tutorial; SECURITY.md names the nested repository, replace refs and the tests copied from git; the assistant takes the person to the access note

requirements.statement: A scheduled or triggered job with no screens has its own work profile, automation, whose capability template is built through the gate and delivered on the local road like any product.
requirements.notes: The owner's goal of 2026-11-23: small things (a single workflow, an automation, an agentic capability) delivered where they must run, through MCP, an API or other integrations; D-0015 and D-0017.

acceptance.given: a two-sentence need for a nightly job reachable over MCP
acceptance.when: its profile is proposed and the product is scaffolded
acceptance.then: the proposal is the automation profile (capability pack, the capability template, ready); its spec guidance reaches the analyst; the product holds app/runtime.json, app/job.py and the faces in factory/ (protected), its Dockerfile copies them and starts through pack_guard, the pack pins them among the runtime files, its own road checks pass on the template, and Rihmasto's static red team finds nothing the web template would not

acceptance.given: an automation project with a builder cell that writes its job, its declaration and a test per criterion
acceptance.when: it is specced, compiled, built and delivered at explore maturity
acceptance.then: the task merges with a passed gate, the release is done on the local preview road, and the running preview answers POST /capability/run and lists its tools over MCP

acceptance.given: a capability whose declaration is not valid, whose job lacks a declared tool's function, or whose routes no longer import the faces
acceptance.when: the product's suite runs at the gate
acceptance.then: the road's capability check for that case fails, so the gate refuses it

requirements.statement: A small capability declares what it needs where it runs (app/runtime.json, rihma.runtime/1), judged deterministically and carried in its capability pack with its secrets by name only.
requirements.notes: The owner's goal of 2026-11-23: small things (a single workflow, an automation, an agentic capability) delivered where they must run, through MCP, an API or other integrations; D-0015 and D-0017.

acceptance.given: declarations with an unknown key, a trigger whose secret is not declared, a schedule out of range, an event pattern outside rihma., a secret given a value, a tool named for a decision, a model role without a workload class, an embed face without origins, an integration naming an undeclared secret, a face named twice, and a string shaped like a live token
acceptance.when: each is validated
acceptance.then: each problem names its JSON path, a valid declaration has none, and the same declaration always gives the same pack section and declaration hash

acceptance.given: a delivered capability release
acceptance.when: its pack is built
acceptance.then: runtime.declared is true with the trigger, faces, tools, model roles, the gateway workloads they call, the agent its openai face offers, integrations and secrets by name (never a value or a reference); a changed declaration changes the pack's content hash; a revision with no declaration says not declared and one with an invalid declaration says not declared with its problems

acceptance.given: capabilities titled with words such as help desk, risk or task, and a declaration whose name and summary hold desk-assistant and risk-assessment
acceptance.when: each is scaffolded and its declaration validated
acceptance.then: the starter declaration is valid and the road's checks pass, no word is taken for a live token, and a token-shaped string that starts a word is still a problem

requirements.statement: One capability image serves several faces (MCP over stdio and Streamable HTTP, an OpenAI-compatible chat also reached through the gateway, a website embed, HTTP), each checked by the pack guard before it answers, with reads and the capability's own tools only.
requirements.notes: The owner's goal of 2026-11-23: small things (a single workflow, an automation, an agentic capability) delivered where they must run, through MCP, an API or other integrations; D-0015 and D-0017.

acceptance.given: the capability's MCP face over stdio and over HTTP
acceptance.when: a client initializes, lists and calls tools, sends a notification, probes server/discover and sends a malformed line
acceptance.then: the protocol version is negotiated, the tools are the two reads then the declared tools in order with the pack's version in _meta, a declared tool runs and an undeclared one is refused (-32602), a wrong argument is an error result, server/discover is method not found, a notification gets no answer (202), stdout carries protocol lines only; over HTTP a set token is required, GET answers 405, an unsupported protocol version 400 and an undeclared Origin 403

acceptance.given: the capability's openai face and a gateway configured from its pack
acceptance.when: a client asks for the capability's name as its model
acceptance.then: the face answers as the capability (another model is 404), the gateway's workload from agent_workloads routes the request to it, --check-pack passes for that config and names an agent routed elsewhere, and a wrong token reaches the client as no upstream answered; a model role the capability declares reaches, through the gateway, the workload its declaration names and the model the pack was accepted with

acceptance.given: a capability with the embed face and declared origins
acceptance.when: the widget, a preflight and a message come from a declared origin, another origin and no origin
acceptance.then: only the declared origin is answered (with CORS for it alone), the widget writes no HTML from data, and a face the declaration does not name answers 404

acceptance.given: the capability started as its image starts it, with its pack and status mounted beside it
acceptance.when: the status is valid, then withdrawn, and an app file is edited
acceptance.then: every face answers once the guard passes and 503 with the guard's reasons once the pack is withdrawn, and with an edited app file MCP over stdio answers a not-ready error

acceptance.given: a delivered capability's openai face, which counts no tokens, and the capability gateway routing to it as the workload of the capability's name
acceptance.when: a chat completion is asked of the face and through the gateway
acceptance.then: the face's usage is null and its rihmasto block says not measured, never zeros, and the gateway's audit records the tokens as not measured

acceptance.given: a capability whose declaration does not name the mcp face, and one that names it but is narrowed by RIHMA_FACES or --face
acceptance.when: MCP over stdio is asked to initialize and list its tools, with --face mcp, with --stdio alone and with no argument
acceptance.then: every request is answered with error -32001 and no tool is listed, while a capability that names the mcp face still answers over stdio

requirements.statement: A verified webhook or a relay event runs a small capability, a schedule runs it on its own, and its result goes out as a signed event the factory's own doorbell accepts.
requirements.notes: The owner's goal of 2026-11-23: small things (a single workflow, an automation, an agentic capability) delivered where they must run, through MCP, an API or other integrations; D-0015 and D-0017.

acceptance.given: a capability started by a webhook whose secret is set
acceptance.when: deliveries arrive signed with Standard Webhooks (kernel/hooks.py), replayed, with a changed body, an old timestamp, another key, an oversized body, and to a capability whose secret is not set
acceptance.then: the verified delivery runs it once with the body as its input, a replay is answered 200 and not run, the others are refused (401, 413, 503) and run nothing

acceptance.given: a capability started by a rihma.signal.received event, subscribed to the relay by IT, with its results sent to a doorbell IT named
acceptance.when: a signal arrives and a relay round runs
acceptance.then: the relay's event runs it, an event of another type runs nothing, and its result goes out as a CloudEvent signed with Standard Webhooks that the factory accepts as one signal with the run's id as its ref, recorded as hook_received

acceptance.given: a scheduled capability served with its schedule on
acceptance.when: it is due, and when its guard does not pass
acceptance.then: it runs on its own when due, and while the guard holds every face it runs nothing

requirements.statement: rihmasto capability serve runs a delivered capability on this machine behind its pack guard and records the trace; capability check judges its declaration; the Compose file carries its faces.
requirements.notes: The owner's goal of 2026-11-23: small things (a single workflow, an automation, an agentic capability) delivered where they must run, through MCP, an API or other integrations; D-0015 and D-0017.

acceptance.given: a delivered capability release
acceptance.when: rihmasto capability serve runs with --face mcp (stdio) and with --face openai --port 0, or with a face it does not offer, no port for an HTTP face, or a release it does not have
acceptance.then: it answers from the release with the pack's version, on 127.0.0.1 only, and the ledger records capability_served with the local user, the pack status that decided it, what was assumed and the pack and declaration hashes; a refusal exits 2 and writes nothing

acceptance.given: a delivered capability release
acceptance.when: rihmasto capability check runs
acceptance.then: it prints the declaration as the pack judges it, writes nothing, and a release it does not have exits 2

acceptance.given: a site's deploy package of a capability release
acceptance.when: its compose.yaml is rendered with the pack's runtime
acceptance.then: its one service carries RIHMA_FACES, the schedule when it is scheduled, every declared secret, the faces' token and the gateway's URL by name only, labels and header lines on how to reach each face; it validates and leaks nothing, and a web product's file is unchanged

acceptance.given: a shell that sets RIHMA_SCHEDULE=on and RIHMA_FACES
acceptance.when: rihmasto capability serve plans the faces process with and without --schedule
acceptance.then: the faces process inherits neither, and capability_served records whether the schedule runs: only with --schedule and a scheduled trigger

requirements.statement: Small capabilities are learnable and reachable (D-0017): the Releases tab shows a capability's runtime and faces, the assistant explains it and takes a person there, and the guide has a tutorial and says what is built and what is planned.
requirements.notes: The owner's goal of 2026-11-23: small things (a single workflow, an automation, an agentic capability) delivered where they must run, through MCP, an API or other integrations; D-0015 and D-0017.

acceptance.given: the cockpit's map and a project with a delivered capability
acceptance.when: a person asks the assistant how the capability is reached
acceptance.then: the map has the capability_faces control on the Releases tab, the answer takes the person to the project's Releases tab and that control, the page carries the control, and the guide has its tutorial and its built and planned lists

requirements.statement: An adopted system is assessed from every perspective: deterministic rules first, each finding with its evidence, severity and suggested change, and 'not measured' where the files cannot tell; the panel's model may propose more, kept apart; the assessment is a versioned record in the ledger, comparable over time and in the evidence pack; and a person turns chosen findings into change cards that go round the change loop.
requirements.notes: The owner's goal of 2026-11-23 for brownfield use: adopt an existing system, get multi-perspective fixes, develop it further. D-0014 (the red team is Rihmasto's own), D-0017 (the same trace on every path; every feature learnable and reachable).

acceptance.given: adopted good and poor fixture repositories (tests/fixtures/assess)
acceptance.when: each is assessed by rule
acceptance.then: the poor one fails rules in each of five perspectives (CI/CD governance, maintenance, security, compliance, architecture and operations), each finding with a severity, a suggested change and its evidence (a file and a line with the masked line, or a measured fact); the good one passes them; branch protection and required checks read 'not measured' with the reason, and nothing that could not be known reads passed

acceptance.given: an adopted repository with a filter, an eol attribute, a link and a credential planted at run time
acceptance.when: it is assessed
acceptance.then: the revision is read from git's objects (no filter runs, the bytes are the blob's, the link is not followed and is said); the red team's static findings are security findings with their rule, CWE and masked evidence; the credential reaches neither the record, the SARIF nor the ledger; what was not read leaves the scan's coverage not measured; and the SARIF beside the record is ingested by the security gate, which the next version counts

acceptance.given: a scripted model
acceptance.when: the intake panel's perspectives review the inventory and the rules' results
acceptance.then: each proposal is model_proposed, numbered apart (P-n), never counted with the rules' findings, with what it rests on checked (found, or not found in the repository); a malformed proposal is dropped and counted; a perspective whose call fails is not measured and the assessment is still recorded; the repository's text cannot close the data fence

acceptance.given: two assessments of a project
acceptance.when: they are recorded
acceptance.then: each is a version AS-n with its sha256 in the index and in the ledger's assessment_recorded record, with the D-0017 trace (who asked, decided by rule, delegated to whom, each assumed check with its reason, the revision and the SARIF's sha256); the second says what is new, resolved, still open and no longer measured, and any two compare; a record changed afterwards shows as not intact; no person, no repository or a bad ref is refused and records nothing

acceptance.given: an assessment
acceptance.when: a person files chosen findings (F-n and P-n)
acceptance.then: each becomes a change card signed by that person with origin 'assessment', triaged by rule as a new requirement that needs a business decision (or the class the person chose), its text naming the evidence, who found it and the suggested change; a finding whose card is still open is skipped; an unknown id, a non-person or an unknown class is refused; each card is assessment_change_opened in the ledger

acceptance.given: the command line
acceptance.when: rihmasto assess and rihmasto assessment list, show, compare and change run
acceptance.then: they assess, list every version with its sha256 checked, show one, compare two and file findings; a refusal exits 2 with the reason on stderr

acceptance.given: the cockpit's API
acceptance.when: a person assesses a project and files findings
acceptance.then: GET .../assessment reads; POST .../assessment assesses, signed by that person: by rule before it answers, with the panel through the cockpit's model in the background (409 without one; 400 without a repository; 403 for a non-person); POST .../assessment/changes files ticked findings as change cards; each write is also a cockpit_write

acceptance.given: an assessed project
acceptance.when: the MCP server and an evidence export read it
acceptance.then: rihma_assessment returns the latest or the named version and writes nothing; the evidence pack carries assessment.json with every version's sha256 checked, and a line in its README

acceptance.given: the cockpit's map and the guide
acceptance.when: a person asks Rihma where to assess a system
acceptance.then: the map's Assessment view and its two controls take the person there; docs/brownfield.md holds the guide, a tutorial and what is built and what is planned

acceptance.given: headless Chrome on the demo home
acceptance.when: a person opens the adopted project's Assessment tab
acceptance.then: they assess it, read its findings by perspective, tick one and file it as a change card, in dark and light, at 1440 and 390 px wide, with keyboard focus and accessible names, and with no console error, failed request or CSP violation

acceptance.given: an adopted system whose suite passed at adoption, and an upstream commit that adds a failing test
acceptance.when: main, the synced upstream and the adoption revision are assessed
acceptance.then: the characterisation baseline reads passed only at the adoption revision its suite ran at; at any other revision it is not measured, with a reason naming both revisions and the result at adoption, it is counted as not measured and listed among what was assumed

acceptance.given: a recorded assessment
acceptance.when: its record and its index entry are edited together so that they agree
acceptance.then: the record is still not intact, because it is checked against the sha256 in the ledger's hash-chained assessment_recorded record: the command line's list, the cockpit's view and the evidence pack (assessment.json and its README line) all say it changed since it was recorded

acceptance.given: a revision holding a file and a folder of the same name, and a credential on a dependency line a rule cites
acceptance.when: it is assessed
acceptance.then: the assessment is recorded and its notes say the file under the folder was not read; the rule's evidence names the file and line with the credential masked, and the credential reaches neither the record nor the ledger

acceptance.given: a package.json and a pyproject.toml that declare no dependency, and two perspectives of the panel that propose the same finding
acceptance.when: the system is assessed with a scripted model and both proposals are filed
acceptance.then: neither manifest is judged: the pinning check names only the requirements file as pinned; each proposal keeps a key naming its perspective, so both are filed as their own change cards and neither is skipped as already open

acceptance.given: a repository whose code reads a hard-coded dict with config.get, names 'audit' as a word and os.environ and an audit_log only in a comment, and whose README mentions privacy in passing; and one that reads os.environ, keeps an audit_log and has a 'Personal data' section
acceptance.when: each is assessed by rule
acceptance.then: the first fails 'configuration comes from the environment', reads the audit trail as not measured and fails 'how personal data is handled is written down'; the second passes all three with the line that shows each, and the personal-data pass says what the section says is not checked by rule

acceptance.given: a scripted model that records which model answered for one perspective of the panel only
acceptance.when: a project is assessed with it
acceptance.then: the record and its trace name that model for that perspective and 'not recorded' for every other

acceptance.given: a mirrored repository
acceptance.when: its revision is read, and a read fails
acceptance.then: the reader of the mirror's objects (git cat-file) has exited and its output is closed in both cases

acceptance.given: an assessed repository with open findings; the owner (2026-11-25): "in the assessment I should be able to ask Rihma what fixes to prioritise and why, and choose select all instead of clicking through each"
acceptance.when: a person asks Ask Rihma which findings to fix first, or opens the Assessment view
acceptance.then: by rule and with no model, the open findings not already filed as an open change come in order (severity, then security and compliance before the rest, then still open since the version before, the panel's opinions after the rules' findings), each with why; the answer takes the person to the assessment; the view offers select the top findings, critical and high, all open, and clear; each finding has its own suggested kind with why, which the person may change, and filing sends each ticked finding's own kind

requirements.statement: A project runs under a posture a person chose (prototype, balanced, production or regulated), tuned by priority weights from 0 to 3 for ux, security, compliance, speed and cost; every effect is a rule in the kernel, previewed before anyone chooses and recorded with who chose it.
requirements.notes: The owner chose presets plus weights (2026-11-23): a posture is one choice that sets how a project runs, changeable per project and during the run; every effect is a rule in the kernel (kernel/posture.py).

acceptance.given: the four postures
acceptance.when: each is previewed (rihmasto posture preview, POST /api/postures/preview)
acceptance.then: prototype is assume mode at explore or demo with autonomy 3 and light gates; balanced is mixed at demo or pilot with autonomy 2 and standard gates; production runs at pilot or production with a security scan and the red team's static layer required, holdouts on staging, IT's deploy gate and an evidence pack; regulated is socratic at any maturity with autonomy 1, plan approval, confirmation by name, warnings blocking, the static and agentic layers and an attestable evidence pack; the same choice always gives the same preview, and a preview writes nothing

acceptance.given: a posture and priority weights
acceptance.when: they are previewed
acceptance.then: they set each perspective's question budget and emphasis, the spec's topics (accessibility for ux on work with screens, threat model for security, record-keeping and data protection for compliance), which findings block and the autonomy; a weight under the posture's floor is raised and the preview says so; an unknown weight or a value outside 0 to 3 is refused

acceptance.given: rihmasto new --posture, or a new project with a posture
acceptance.when: the project is made
acceptance.then: its mode and maturity are the posture's unless named; a maturity it does not run at or a looser mode is refused as a usage error and nothing is made; posture_chosen records the person, persona, weights and the preview they were shown; without a posture the project is made exactly as before

requirements.statement: The posture acts on the intake, the spec and the plan, by rule.
requirements.notes: The owner chose presets plus weights (2026-11-23): a posture is one choice that sets how a project runs, changeable per project and during the run; every effect is a rule in the kernel (kernel/posture.py).

acceptance.given: a project with a posture
acceptance.when: the panel reads its request
acceptance.then: each perspective's prompt carries its question budget and what it weighs, and no perspective files more questions than its budget

acceptance.given: a posture whose weights require topics
acceptance.when: the spec is written and the plan reviewed
acceptance.then: the analyst's prompt carries each topic's guidance and one more requirement per topic; the kernel checks coverage by rule and a spec that misses a topic waits for a person at any maturity, with the missing topic on the plan card; a person's edit that covers it counts at once

acceptance.given: a confirming posture (regulated, or compliance 3)
acceptance.when: it runs to the build
acceptance.then: every question is settled by a person before the spec, a person approves the plan at any maturity, approving confirms each requirement no named person confirmed in the approver's name (requirements_confirmed), and an open assumption holds the build until a person confirms or refutes it

requirements.statement: How much waits for a person follows the posture's autonomy, beneath the autonomy cap.
requirements.notes: The owner chose presets plus weights (2026-11-23): a posture is one choice that sets how a project runs, changeable per project and during the run; every effect is a rule in the kernel (kernel/posture.py).

acceptance.given: a posture whose autonomy is below a step's level
acceptance.when: the factory would build or deliver
acceptance.then: the step waits for one go-ahead card per step and revision; a person's approval lets it go on; a declined card asks again with the decline in its body; the autonomy cap still refuses a step above it

acceptance.given: a balanced project from an idea
acceptance.when: the pipeline runs it
acceptance.then: it stops at its blocking question, the go-ahead to build and the go-ahead to deliver, each decided by a named person and recorded in the ledger in that order, before the release starts

requirements.statement: The posture decides which signals block a release.
requirements.notes: The owner chose presets plus weights (2026-11-23): a posture is one choice that sets how a project runs, changeable per project and during the run; every effect is a rule in the kernel (kernel/posture.py).

acceptance.given: a posture that requires a scan
acceptance.when: the security gate is asked before a landing
acceptance.then: it holds the release until a security scan and the red team's static layer were ingested, and the agentic layer where the project has an active embed; each missing one is named with the command that provides it; warnings block at security 3; a preview or demo landing is held too; without a posture nothing changes

acceptance.given: a release past IT's deploy gate under a posture with evidence
acceptance.when: it would enter production
acceptance.then: it waits until an evidence pack is exported for that release (attestable where the posture asks it), and a pack's security summary reports the findings alone

requirements.statement: A posture changed during the run says what it changes now and later, never silently.

acceptance.then: a subscription IT has not marked as a sandbox receiver gets a digest without that project's title or reasons, only how many projects were left out; a sandbox receiver gets it listed; the relay's record names the projects held

acceptance.given: a project with a track
acceptance.when: a person opens it in the cockpit, or reads its track
acceptance.then: the project header shows one on-track answer (the Track pill, never beside a health chip with the same words) and the Health card shows that same answer; the track carries every reason the health reads, so an approval gone stale or a last release that stopped makes it at risk

requirements.statement: Any input, from any author, is read for what it is: what it states is kept as given with its lines and never asked again, the facet checklist finds the gaps and the mode settles them, and the intake summary shows from your input, asked and assumed side by side.
requirements.notes: D-0017: every path writes the same trace (who asked, what was given, what was assumed, what proves it), and the feature is learnable and reachable (docs/guides/inputs.md, cockpit/ui_map.json). Kernel: kernel/input_kind.py, kernel/input_facets.py, kernel/input_intake.py, kernel/input_summary.py.

acceptance.given: a one-line need, a two-line Finnish need, an expert's specification with ids and criteria, a full plan with three deliberate gaps, and a folder of mixed documents (tests/fixtures/inputs)
acceptance.when: each is read by rule
acceptance.then: each is read as its kind (need, need, specification, plan, folder) with its language and the rules that decided it; a folder's documents are each read as their own kind; a long text with no structure is a need, read as uncertain

acceptance.given: the same inputs
acceptance.when: the facet checklist reads them
acceptance.then: every fact the input states is kept with its facet, document and lines, quoting the author's own words; the gaps are exactly the facets it does not state (all thirteen for the one-line need; data and its sensitivity, availability and acceptance criteria for the plan); the author's requirements keep their ids, statements and given / when / then criteria, and a plan's decisions their lines; a section that says only TBD leaves its facet open, with its lines

acceptance.given: an intake whose panel asks again what the input states
acceptance.when: the panel's questions are screened
acceptance.then: a question every facet of which the input states is not asked, and is recorded with the facts it rests on, in the reading and the ledger; the panel is told, word for word in one shared prefix, what the input states and what its gaps are; for a need, the profile's standing questions are still asked

acceptance.given: a specification, a plan or a folder in socratic, assume or mixed mode
acceptance.when: intake runs
acceptance.then: the checklist asks its own question for each gap no question covers, from the maturity that needs it (and as a posture preset changes that); socratic puts every asked question to a person, assume assumes each with a due date, mixed sends the blocking gaps (users and roles, outcomes, scope, data) to a person and assumes the rest; a need's gaps are the panel's to ask, so the checklist adds none

acceptance.given: an expert's specification and a plan
acceptance.when: the spec is written from the analyst's draft, and the plan is taken in
acceptance.then: each of the author's requirements keeps its id, its statement and its criteria word for word, with the draft's criterion kinds by place, as customer-endorsed by whoever asked; one the draft left out is kept as written and marked restored; the contract compiles from them; a plan's decisions arrive as given in the brief, never as an assumption, a question or a decision in the canon

acceptance.given: a recorded reading
acceptance.when: a named person asks the analyst's model to refine it
acceptance.then: the model's proposal is kept as model_proposed beside the rule's reading, with only the facets and lines the kernel checked and quoted itself, and what it left out with why; it changes no kind, question or decision; a model is never the one who asks; when no model answers it is not measured and nothing is written; in a folder a cited line is placed in its own document

acceptance.given: a project whose input was read
acceptance.when: a person asks for the intake summary on the command line or through the cockpit's API
acceptance.then: the summary sets from your input (facts, decisions, requirements with their lines), asked (with the answer and who gave it) and assumed (with the assumption and its due date) side by side, beside the questions not asked and every facet's state; `rihmasto inputs summary` prints it as JSON or text and `rihmasto inputs read` reads a request without writing; the ledger records who asked, the kind, every fact with its lines and the request's sha256, and the screening

acceptance.given: the cockpit on a project whose plan was taken in
acceptance.when: a person opens its Questions view in Chrome
acceptance.then: the intake summary shows its three columns side by side at 1440 px and stacked at 390 px with no sideways scroll, in light and dark; its regions are named by their headings; Tab reaches its first link and Enter opens that question; the facet checklist opens from the keyboard; Ask Rihma's Take me there brings the person to it; and no console error or CSP violation occurs

acceptance.when: the panel's questions are screened
acceptance.then: a question with any word of its own that the stated facts of its facets and the input's titles do not hold (deleting a tool, an email reminder, working offline, the tests before a release) is asked; only a question that restates is not asked; a blocking question that restates is still asked, so the mode can put it to a person, with its rationale citing the facts and their lines, and the reading and the ledger record it as restated

Skip".

acceptance.then: each is listed as skipped: may hold secrets (never opened by its name, or its text holds a credential), and no secret appears in the request, the material map, the ledger, the panel's prompts, a snapshot or the cockpit page

acceptance.given: a folder whose documents are larger than the budget, and exclusions by path, glob and folder
acceptance.when: it is scanned
acceptance.then: the most telling files are read first (the README, briefs and specs, then plans, reviews, handovers and the code inventory, then notes and slides, then data and logs), a long one is summarised to its first part and the rest are listed, every cut is named in the map's cut notes with why, the request never exceeds the budget, dependency, build, cache, virtual environment and version-control folders are not walked, and the person's exclusions are skipped with the pattern that dropped them

acceptance.given: a folder given as intake's source
acceptance.when: intake runs
acceptance.then: the request is built from the material map, each part headed with its file path and kind; the map is kept in the project (material.json) and the ledger records its counts, never a file's contents; the any-input reading reads each part as its own document; a request confirmed from a scan arrives as text and keeps its documents by the map's digest

acceptance.given: a person at the command line
acceptance.when: they run rihmasto scan on a folder, and rihmasto new with that folder as the source
acceptance.then: scan prints what would be read, summarised, listed and skipped and why, the characters it comes to and where they would go; new shows the same map and creates nothing and sends nothing without --yes or a yes at the terminal; with it the map is recorded with the person and how they confirmed, and --exclude drops files

acceptance.given: the cockpit's New project dialog
acceptance.when: a person asks for a folder's preview, or creates or adopts a project from a scanned folder
acceptance.then: POST /api/source/preview answers a named person with a persona that may create or adopt a project, only for a folder under the home or a configured root, never a system folder or a folder of keys, and records nothing; the files the person unticked travel with the create and adopt requests, a created project keeps the map the person saw with who confirmed it, and its request leaves the unticked files out

acceptance.given: a project marked confidential: keep on local models, and a role routed to a hosted endpoint
acceptance.when: intake, the spec, the holdouts, a build, a change's triage, a refinement or a run would call a model for it
acceptance.then: the call is refused before anything is sent, with the role and its endpoint named and how to configure a local model (docs/guides/local-models.md), the refusal is recorded, a run stops in a refused state and the cockpit and the command line refuse before a project is created; the setting is recorded in the ledger; with every role on loopback or a private address the work goes on

acceptance.given: An existing project given as a git repository, a folder with code that is not a git repository, or a folder of documents only
acceptance.when: it is adopted
acceptance.then: a git repository is adopted as before and its documents are scanned as context; a folder that is not one is snapshotted into a new git repository under the factory home with only the files that pass the scan's rules, committed as the baseline and adopted from there, and the person's folder is never changed; a folder with no code is refused with the offer to start a new project from it as material

acceptance.given: a person in the cockpit in a real browser, light and dark, 1440 and 390 px wide
acceptance.when: they give New project a folder, scan it, untick a file and adopt it, and give it a folder of documents only
acceptance.then: the scan step shows the map grouped by read, summarised, unticked, listed and skipped with each reason, unticking scans again without the file and keeps the focus on it, adopt starts the job with the exclusion, a documents-only folder is offered as material for a new project and created from it; no secret is on the page, nothing scrolls sideways, and there is no console error, failed request or CSP violation

acceptance.given: a confidential project whose role's primary endpoint is local and whose fallback is hosted, and one whose primary is hosted
acceptance.when: the project's intake, spec, holdouts, build, refinement, change or assistant asks that role
acceptance.then: the local role is not refused: the hosted fallback is skipped and never called, because the lanes the project's calls run in (the analyst lane, the assistant's, the product surface and an adopted project's) are compiled without it, so no request reaches a hosted endpoint even when the local one fails; the ledger records confidential_fallback_skipped once per run, naming the role and the host; a role whose primary endpoint is hosted is refused as before

acceptance.when: a release is built for a tag that is not v1.2.0, is not a version, or for a version the changelog has no section for
acceptance.then: the build is refused with the reason and no file is written

acceptance.given: a checkout whose pyproject.toml declares 1.2.0 and whose changelog has a [1.2.0] section
acceptance.when: a release is built for the tag v1.2.0
acceptance.then: it holds a .tar.gz and a .zip of the files git tracks at HEAD under rihmasto-1.2.0/, a CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM naming rihmasto 1.2.0, its licence, the archives' hashes and Gnomon as its one runtime dependency, SHA256SUMS that verify, and the notes word for word from the [1.2.0] section; building again from the same commit gives the same bytes

acceptance.given: a declared version that is an alpha, beta, release candidate or development version

acceptance.given: the release workflow
