acceptance.then: the suite and the contract run before anything is built; the provenance attestation and the GitHub Release happen only for a pushed tag; the workflow reads by default, only the publishing job may write contents, no expression is expanded inside a script, and a run by hand publishes nothing

requirements.statement: A person can see and set which model answers for each of Rihmasto's roles: an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, a model name and an API key given as an environment variable's name or stored outside the repository, never shown again, never logged and never in the ledger; a Test sends a tiny prompt and says the latency or the error; changes go to this machine's routing overlay, never to the shipped routing.
requirements.notes: The owner: "is there now way for me to input the model endpoint / api for the platform itself?" kernel/models_setup.py, kernel/shape_cli.py (`rihmasto models`), cockpit/shape_routes.py, cockpit/static/models.js, docs/guides/models-setup.md. Presets: llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM on this machine, OpenCode Go, OpenAI, OpenRouter, another OpenAI-compatible provider. Every real model call still goes through Gnomon; Test is the one direct call. FR-MDL1-AC-10 came with the owner's decisions of 2026-11-24 after a journey test ("1. Yes 2. Skip 3. Agreed 4. Ask"), which saw the builder called on a hosted endpoint while Models setup said its key was not set: Gnomon held it (`gnomon key set`, its credential store per packages/gnomon-core/src/credentials.ts).

acceptance.given: the routing with its roles
acceptance.when: a person opens Models setup
acceptance.then: every role the routing defines is shown with its model, family, endpoint host, whether it is local or hosted, the name of its key variable and whether a key is set (never the key), its fallback and whether it answers

acceptance.given: a role, an endpoint and a key
acceptance.when: a person sets the role, with the key given to be stored, or by its variable's name, or a change the routing's rules refuse
acceptance.then: the role, its endpoint and the model's family are written to kernel/routing.local.json and the shipped routing.json is unchanged; a stored key is kept in a secrets file outside the repository and handed to Gnomon in the variable the endpoint names; the ledger records who set which role to which host and how the key is found, never the key; a refused change (the verifier's family, an address that is not http(s), a key typed as its variable's name, not a person) writes nothing

acceptance.given: a role pointed at an endpoint
acceptance.when: a person presses Test
acceptance.then: a tiny prompt is sent to the endpoint with its key, and the answer's latency is shown, or the error (a refused key, nothing answering, no key set) with the key scrubbed; nothing is recorded

acceptance.given: a role set on this machine

acceptance.then: its overlay entry goes, with the endpoint and the stored key only it used, and the ledger records who did it

acceptance.given: the command line

acceptance.then: each does what the page does and no output holds the key; a change by something that is not a person is refused

acceptance.given: the cockpit
acceptance.when: a person sets, tests and removes a role, and Home asks whether a model answers
acceptance.then: the routes are signed writes like the others (Test records nothing), the answers never hold the key, a refused change says why and writes nothing, and Home's Set up a model card shows while no model Rihma talks with answers

acceptance.given: the cockpit's map

acceptance.then: it takes them to Models setup, whose view and controls are in the map with labels of their own

acceptance.given: a model server on the owner's own network: this machine, a private or link-local address, a tailnet address (100.64.0.0/10), or a host reached by name that the owner declares private in Models setup
acceptance.when: a confidential project's role is routed to it, or Models setup shows it
acceptance.then: it counts as local and the project may use it; a host reached by name that is not declared private, or a public address, counts as hosted and is refused for confidential work

acceptance.given: an endpoint whose key variable is set neither in the environment nor in Models setup's store, while Gnomon holds a key for it (gnomon key set)
acceptance.when: Models setup or rihmasto doctor shows it
acceptance.then: it reads "key set by Gnomon", not "no key", by asking `gnomon key list`, which prints names only; when Gnomon cannot say but its credential store exists, it reads "Gnomon may have its own key for this host"; Rihmasto never opens the store or reads a key's value, and Test says it cannot send a key Gnomon holds

requirements.statement: Anything set when a project was made can change: a person changes its kind of work, mode, maturity or title with a preview of what the change means for the work already done, sends it back to its material, questions, spec or plan so that step runs again, and adds material later; nothing is deleted, every change is signed and recorded, and a project always says what it waits for, who can act and the actions that move it forward.
requirements.notes: The owner, using Rihmasto daily on a customer project: "I don't want to see stupid mistakes like me choosing a template for the project or me generating a spec, then I'm getting stuck somewhere because Rihmasto assumed the project template wrong. I want all that to be able to change." kernel/project_settings.py, kernel/rewind.py, kernel/project_material.py, kernel/next_step.py, kernel/change_cli.py, cockpit/static/change.js, docs/guides/change-anything.md. The posture has its own change flow (kernel/posture_change.py) and is not changed here. FR-CHG1-AC-11 to AC-13 were decided by the owner on 2026-11-24 after a journey test walked their real flows ("1. Yes 2. Skip 3. Agreed 4. Ask"): AC-11 is "1. Yes", AC-12 and AC-13 are "3. Agreed" (kernel/go_ahead.py).

acceptance.given: a project whose intake ran for one kind of work, with an open question
acceptance.when: a person changes its kind of work with a reason, after a preview, and asks to go back
acceptance.then: the preview writes nothing and says the open questions no longer fit; project_changed records the person, persona, reason, before and after; the open questions are withdrawn with their cards decided as withdrawn and the reason; settled answers are kept; and the next run asks the questions again for the new kind without asking a settled one again

acceptance.given: a project whose spec is written
acceptance.when: a person changes its maturity and asks to go back
acceptance.then: the impact says the spec was written for the old maturity and whether a person now approves the plan; the spec is kept as a superseded version and written again at the next run

acceptance.given: a project whose questions wait on people
acceptance.when: a person changes its mode
acceptance.then: nothing is settled unless the person asks; when asked, each open question the new mode lets the factory assume is assumed in that person's name; a change by a non-person, a persona that may not, with no reason or to a value no setting takes is refused and writes nothing

acceptance.given: a project compiled from its spec
acceptance.when: a person sends it back to the plan, the spec, the questions and the material in turn
acceptance.then: each step's files are moved under superseded/ and listed, never deleted; the ledger records rewound with the person, persona and reason; and the pipeline's next tick runs that step again (compile, spec, intake), or waits for material

acceptance.given: a project with a release
acceptance.when: a person asks to send it back to any step
acceptance.then: it is refused with a message that names the release and the change loop, and nothing changes; a settings change still records the new value and goes back nowhere

acceptance.given: a project whose intake ran and a question was answered
acceptance.when: a person adds material with re-intake
acceptance.then: the original request is kept and the material is appended under its own heading and kept with its sha256 in material.json and the ledger; the panel reads only the new material, told what was asked before, and only questions not on record are added and settled by the mode; every answer stands; from the cockpit the panel reads it in the next run; only scripted models answer in the test

acceptance.given: any state a project can be in
acceptance.when: next_step reads it
acceptance.then: every state the pipeline returns maps to at least one action naming who may take it and the control, view or command that carries it out; the records' own states (no material, blocking questions, decision cards, paused, a model endpoint that failed, an intake to run again, a stopped build, released, adopted, attached, running) each name their waits, who and actions

acceptance.given: the cockpit and the command line
acceptance.when: a person changes the settings, goes back a step, adds material or asks what is next
acceptance.then: PUT settings, POST settings/preview, rewind and material are signed by a person and persona, checked for access like every write route, recorded in the project's ledger (the preview records nothing), refuse a project a job runs for or with a release, and `rihmasto settings`, `rewind`, `material add` and `next` do the same

acceptance.given: the cockpit in a browser
acceptance.when: a person follows What's next, changes the kind with its preview, adds material, goes back a step and advances
acceptance.then: each write lands signed with their name; dark and light at 1440 and 390 pixels wide the overview and the three dialogs fit with nothing scrolling sideways, every control has an accessible name, and no step leaves a console error, a failed request or a Content-Security-Policy violation

acceptance.given: a project whose spec is written, and material added to it with re-intake, or a blocking question opened after the spec
acceptance.when: the project is advanced
acceptance.then: the run stops once the panel has read the material, waiting on its new blocking questions or on a person's choice to go back to the spec or go on with it as it is, and nothing is built past an open blocking question; What's next names those choices

acceptance.given: a project whose questions a person answered, a person let the factory assume, and the factory assumed on its own by its mode or a default
acceptance.when: a person changes its kind of work and goes back to the questions
acceptance.then: the settings preview says how many answers and assumptions a person chose are kept and how many open questions and assumptions the factory made on its own are withdrawn; saving withdraws those assumptions (question and assumption) with the reason "made for the old kind", keeps every one a person chose, and the panel that runs again is told only the person-settled ones; the records still agree with the ledger

acceptance.given: a project made by a person (New project, rihmasto new, Shape it in chat) at explore or demo maturity, whose spec is written and never built
acceptance.when: it is advanced
acceptance.then: the run waits once on a "Look at the spec before building" card with Go and Skip, shown in What's next and the Inbox; either verdict lets the build start, signed; "Build without waiting for me" (Project settings, New project, --build-without-waiting) turns it off for the project and withdraws an open card; a delegation's go rule may say Go; at pilot and up the plan's approval stays the look; a project made without saying, and the scripted demo, which sets it off explicitly, build as before

acceptance.given: the cockpit in a real browser, dark and light, 1440 and 390 px wide
acceptance.when: a person ticks Build without waiting for me in New project, previews a new kind of work in Project settings, and says Go on the Look at the spec card in What's next
acceptance.then: the option reaches the project, the preview counts what is kept and withdrawn, the Go lands signed and the card is decided; nothing scrolls sideways, every control has an accessible name, and there is no console error, failed request or CSP violation

requirements.statement: A product declares the data systems it reaches (databases, data warehouses, cloud storage, ERPs and business APIs by OpenAPI, MCP servers, REST APIs), each with how it is reached, its access, its data classes and its credentials by name only; the spec and the plan list them, and each becomes a requirement a test must name (D-0015, D-0017).

acceptance.given: declarations with an unknown kind, a way the kind does not allow, an access other than read or read-write, an unknown data class, an openapi one with no system, a credential that does not start with its settings' prefix or is a setting, a name whose settings would look like a secret or a road setting, an unknown key, or a secret-looking value
acceptance.when: they are validated, by the kernel or the command line
acceptance.then: each break is named by its JSON path, the command line refuses a broken declaration with exit 2 and lists every kind with its reference connector, and a valid declaration is declared

acceptance.given: an analyst's draft that declares integrations
acceptance.when: the spec is made and compiled
acceptance.then: each valid one reaches spec.json with a provenance by the spec's rules, an invalid or repeated one is dropped with its reason, each becomes an INT- requirement whose one test criterion names it in a fixed form that reads back from the compiled contract for every kind and way, and spec.md, the plan card and the ledger's spec_written list them with their access, data classes, settings and credential names

acceptance.given: an open plan
acceptance.when: a person declares or withdraws an integration
acceptance.then: only a named person with a plan editor's persona may; the declaration is theirs (customer-confirmed), the plan's version moves on, its open card is withdrawn, the ledger records who, as which persona and why, a redrafted spec keeps it, and it is refused once the plan is compiled; a plan whose product writes to a system it reaches, or touches confidential or restricted data there, waits for a person's approval at any maturity

acceptance.given: a spec with integrations
acceptance.when: the cockpit shows its plan
acceptance.then: the Plan view and the plan's approval card list each integration with its way, access and data classes (the integrations control in the cockpit's map), and Ask Rihma takes a person there

requirements.statement: IT binds each declared integration to a concrete endpoint and secret references on the paved road of each environment and approves each binding on a road card; delivery wires the approved ones into the deploy package and the Compose file as settings and secrets by name (D-0015).

acceptance.given: bindings that are missing, give an endpoint of the wrong scheme for the way or plain http off loopback, carry a password or a token in the endpoint or its query, give a secret a value or no reference, name a credential the declaration does not, or hold an unknown key
acceptance.when: they are checked against the declaration
acceptance.then: each problem is named, a valid binding has none, a road may bind each environment differently, and the binding's pin changes when the binding does

acceptance.given: a release whose product declares an integration
acceptance.when: it is delivered
acceptance.then: before anything is built, a road card that only IT decides shows what it reaches, the access, the data classes, the endpoint and where each credential lives, one card per binding and not one per call; configured lets the release go on, declined stops it, and a binding changed since withdraws the open card and opens a new one that names any problem

acceptance.given: an approved binding
acceptance.when: the deploy package and the site's Compose file are made
acceptance.then: the package lists the integration with the card that approved it and its settings, each credential as a secret reference and never a value; Compose gives each setting, and each secret by its name from the deployer's environment; a package whose integration no card approved, or whose endpoint carries a credential, is refused; a local process gets an env: secret's value (a docker product: FR-DS5)

requirements.statement: The gate runs a product's own tests against stand-ins for the integrations its contract declares, and its integrations signal says whether the product's data access held to the declaration.

acceptance.given: a contract that declares an integration
acceptance.when: the gate runs the product's suite
acceptance.then: the integration's settings point at a stand-in (a SQLite file seeded from the product's seed, or a loopback HTTP server answering from the product's fixture) with placeholder credentials, and a product whose INT- test reads through it is merged with the integrations signal passed

acceptance.given: an integration declared read
acceptance.when: the product's tests write to it
acceptance.then: the integrations signal fails and names the write (the SQLite file changed; a PUT, PATCH or DELETE; a POST that is not a read query; an MCP tool whose name writes), and the change is not merged although its tests pass; a read-write object-store stand-in round-trips what the product puts

acceptance.given: a task whose INT- test never reaches its HTTP stand-in, or an INT- criterion edited so that it no longer names its integration
acceptance.when: the gate runs
acceptance.then: the integrations signal is not measured, with the reason; a contract that declares no integration starts no stand-in and adds no signal

requirements.statement: Reference connectors reach PostgreSQL, Snowflake, S3-compatible storage and ERPs or business APIs by OpenAPI through Gnomon, read-only first, each passing the connector contract suite against a local fake (D-0015).

acceptance.given: connectors/postgres, snowflake, s3 and openapi
acceptance.when: the contract suite runs
acceptance.then: each validates with no write tool, its forbidden tools listed, its credentials by reference and a local fake of its system; postgres runs its pinned server in restricted mode, snowflake pins its read-only service configuration, and what could not be confirmed offline is marked UNVERIFIED

acceptance.given: each connector's fake
acceptance.when: the suite runs against it
acceptance.then: a pinned vendor server faked in process answers its pin, its reads map to valid proposals of the declared kind, a write and a forbidden tool are refused and a rug pull is caught; a narrow server reads its fake backend signed (SigV4 for S3, a bearer token for the API), sends only GET and HEAD, is refused with the wrong credentials, refuses a write tool, a write operation and an endpoint that is not https or loopback, and no write reaches the backend

acceptance.given: the PostgreSQL live check
acceptance.when: it is run
acceptance.then: it runs only with RIHMA_LIVE_POSTGRES=1 and a DSN whose host is loopback, and is skipped otherwise with the reason; against a real database it checks the pinned tools/list, that the reads map to valid proposals, and that a statement that writes is refused and leaves nothing behind

requirements.statement: A product on the docker road gets each approved integration's credential whose reference is env: by name only (docker run --env NAME), its value read on the deploying host at deploy time and handed to the docker CLI in that command's environment, so no argument, package or record holds it (D-0014, D-0015).

acceptance.given: an approved integration whose credential lives in env: on the deploying host, and a docker road
acceptance.when: the product is deployed, with that variable set on the host and again without it
acceptance.then: docker run gets the integration's settings as values and the credential as --env NAME with no value in any argument, the value reaches the docker CLI's environment for that command only, no file in the project holds it, and a credential the host does not hold is not given

acceptance.given: a declaration whose name, and so its settings and credentials, start like a variable the deploy tools read (DOCKER_HOST, DOCKER_CONFIG, HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY, SSL_CERT_FILE, LD_PRELOAD and the rest of their families), a binding of one, a package that carries one approved before, and a docker run handed one
acceptance.when: it is declared, its binding is checked, the package is validated, or the docker CLI is to run
acceptance.then: the declaration is refused at /name, the binding has a problem that names the credential so no card can approve it, the package fails validation so it is not delivered, and the docker CLI refuses before it runs, so no such value ever reaches the CLI's own environment; a plain credential still does

requirements.statement: A person states a goal in a project in their own words, in English or Finnish, and Rihma answers with a plan grounded in the project's records and in a catalogue of what this Rihmasto can do read from its code at run time, with honest gaps; each step is one action the person takes with one click, and nothing is written until a person takes a step that writes, signed, through the existing routes.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24): "I described a case of trying to work with a project in Rihmasto and was unclear what to do with it. I shouldn't be left in the dark in Rihmasto: if I have a question like 'I want to hook this solution to Google Drive', I should get agentic help for that. Essentially all visible work I do in projects, as well as insights feeding from Rihmasto to the terminal / IDE / Claude / Codex / OpenCode / whatever agents are actually developing: configurations and insights, feedback from Rihmasto towards agents, Rihmasto using its own agents to deliver a capability or package, or agents checking for feedback, plans and assessments done in Rihmasto." kernel/copilot.py, kernel/copilot_steps.py, kernel/copilot_catalog.py, cockpit/static/goal.js, docs/guides/agentic-help.md.

acceptance.given: an adopted project, no model, and the goal 'I want to hook this solution to Google Drive' (and the same goals in Finnish, and goals to run it nightly in the cloud, deploy to test, add sign-in, monitor it and give it to a coding agent)
acceptance.when: Rihma plans it
acceptance.then: the goals are recognised by rule; the Google Drive plan has a drafted change request with the goal and the questions it raises, the gap that no Google Drive connector exists with the options, a REST integration step, where it runs (the deployment road), a schedule automation and a hand-off to a coding agent; every step is one of the allowed action kinds with a route the cockpit has; nothing is written

acceptance.given: a factory with a configured docker road, a connector folder IT has not enabled, and the streams this build has or lacks
acceptance.when: a plan is made for a goal that reaches that system or a road
acceptance.then: the catalogue names the configured road and its environments, the connector and its state with the command IT enables it with, the declared integration kind, and marks a step whose feature is not in this build as not available yet with the reason

acceptance.given: a scripted assistant model, and a confidential project whose assistant model is hosted
acceptance.when: a goal is planned with the model
acceptance.then: the model's steps are checked: an unknown kind, a route the cockpit lacks or a command that is not one plain rihmasto command is dropped with its reason, a claim that it acted is taken out; the confidential project gets the rule-based plan, the model is never asked, and the note says how to fix it in Models setup

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma in a project
acceptance.when: a person states a goal, asks where something is, or asks how the project is doing
acceptance.then: the goal gets the plan in the answer, the others keep the map and the status answers

acceptance.given: the cockpit in headless Chrome, dark and light, 1440 and 390 pixels wide
acceptance.when: a person asks Ask Rihma to hook the project to Google Drive and presses Draft it on the plan
acceptance.then: the plan shows its gap and steps, the change form opens prefilled with the goal, filing it opens a change card signed with the person's name, nothing scrolls sideways and no console error is left

acceptance.given: an adopted project and a configured gcp-cloudrun road for production
acceptance.when: a person asks to hook it to Google Drive and run it in Google Cloud
acceptance.then: the plan has no gap: it declares a Google Drive integration (kind gdrive, through the road's own Drive client) and runs on the configured Google Cloud road

requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24): "I described a case of trying to work with a project in Rihmasto and was unclear what to do with it. I shouldn't be left in the dark in Rihmasto: if I have a question like 'I want to hook this solution to Google Drive', I should get agentic help for that. Essentially all visible work I do in projects, as well as insights feeding from Rihmasto to the terminal / IDE / Claude / Codex / OpenCode / whatever agents are actually developing: configurations and insights, feedback from Rihmasto towards agents, Rihmasto using its own agents to deliver a capability or package, or agents checking for feedback, plans and assessments done in Rihmasto." kernel/agent_bridge.py, kernel/agent_writes.py, mcp/bridge_tools.py, kernel/bridge_cli.py, cockpit/bridge_routes.py, cockpit/static/goal.js, cockpit/static/agents.js.

acceptance.given: a project with a contract, open questions and assumptions, a change card naming one requirement and a failed gate
acceptance.when: a hand-off brief is built for the change, for each agent, and from the command line
acceptance.then: the brief holds the change, only that requirement's criteria, the open questions and assumptions, the plan, the failed gate, how to run the tests and how to report back; each agent gets its prompt file, MCP configuration and command line (claude -p, codex exec, opencode run, Cursor's MCP file); building it writes nothing and recording a hand-off notes who, to which agent and the brief's sha256

acceptance.given: Rihma's MCP server over the stdio protocol
acceptance.when: an agent calls rihma_next, rihma_plan, rihma_questions, rihma_handoff, rihma_feedback, rihma_insights, rihma_alignment and rihma_health
acceptance.then: each answers from the records without an error, and a part not in this build says it is not available yet

acceptance.given: an agent connected over MCP as its operator
acceptance.when: it posts progress, proposes an answer to an open question, and requests the gate on an attached repository and on a project the factory builds
acceptance.then: each write names the agent and its operator in the ledger and the channel, the question stays open as a proposal, the attached repository's gate runs signed as the operator and its result posts itself, the factory-built project is refused with why, and no card is decided

acceptance.given: the cockpit in headless Chrome, dark and light, 1440 and 390 pixels wide
acceptance.when: a person opens a project whose agents posted progress and presses Hand off to an agent
acceptance.then: the Agents working on this strip shows the agent's posts, hand-offs and gate results; the dialog shows the brief and each agent's way to use it; copying records the hand-off; nothing scrolls sideways and no console error is left

requirements.statement: Each project has an agent channel: one threaded conversation between people, Rihma's own agents and the external coding agents, with every post recorded without its text in the ledger; Rihma's agents answer questions addressed to them from the records by rule, else through Gnomon in the matching role with a trace, within limits that stop two agents looping; a person watches it live, steps in, confirms or rejects proposals and pauses it, and an Agent activity monitor lists the live channels across the factory.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24): "I described a case of trying to work with a project in Rihmasto and was unclear what to do with it. I shouldn't be left in the dark in Rihmasto: if I have a question like 'I want to hook this solution to Google Drive', I should get agentic help for that. Essentially all visible work I do in projects, as well as insights feeding from Rihmasto to the terminal / IDE / Claude / Codex / OpenCode / whatever agents are actually developing: configurations and insights, feedback from Rihmasto towards agents, Rihmasto using its own agents to deliver a capability or package, or agents checking for feedback, plans and assessments done in Rihmasto." And: "per project, the Rihma agents should be able to do this back and forth with terminal or IDE agents, and me being able to track it, in a chat window or some agent tracing / monitoring." kernel/agent_channel.py, kernel/channel_rihma.py, mcp/bridge_tools.py, kernel/bridge_cli.py, cockpit/bridge_routes.py, cockpit/static/agents.js.

acceptance.given: two fake external agents, each over its own MCP stdio server and operator
acceptance.when: they post progress, read the channel, post a question to @verifier and ask Rihma what a criterion means
acceptance.then: Rihma's analyst answers the criterion from the contract and the verifier the gate from the ledger, each with its sources; each agent sees the other's posts; every post is in the ledger as channel_posted with ids, author and kind and never its text

acceptance.given: a scripted model for Rihma's agents, and a confidential project whose model is hosted
acceptance.when: an agent asks something the rules cannot answer, once pointing at a commit
acceptance.then: the analyst (the verifier, for the commit) answers through the model with a trace naming the role, the model and how long it took, a claim that it acted is taken out; the confidential project's question is answered without asking the model, saying how to fix it in Models setup

acceptance.given: an agent's proposed answer to an open question in the channel
acceptance.when: a person confirms it in the cockpit, and rejects another
acceptance.then: the confirmed one answers the question with its text signed by the person through the Questions view's route and the message says confirmed by whom; the rejected one leaves its question open

acceptance.given: an agent asking Rihma
acceptance.when: it asks the same question again, asks more than the hourly cap in a thread, and posts while a person has paused the channel
acceptance.then: the repeat gets one pointer to the first answer and then silence, the cap gets one note and then silence, a post while paused waits unanswered and hidden from agents until a person resumes the channel

acceptance.given: the command line

acceptance.then: the post is signed and recorded, a question to @analyst is answered, and the channel prints line by line with authors, kinds and references

requirements.statement: IT can configure a gcp-cloudrun paved road (Google Cloud projects per environment, a region, an Artifact Registry repository, the identity Rihmasto deploys as and the one the product runs as, network and egress, Secret Manager secrets by name) on which a product runs as a Cloud Run service or as a Cloud Run job that Cloud Scheduler runs on a schedule with retries; the road renders and validates the exact YAML and gcloud commands, deploys to the test environment first and to production only through IT's deploy gate, promotes and rolls back by revision or by image, reads a job's executions into its probes, and runs gcloud only when it is on PATH and signed in and the road is configured, saying exactly what is missing otherwise.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24), on an adopted project, an agentic workflow that transcribes recordings: it must be "taken into the company's Google Cloud, to be run regularly, to read recordings in Google Drive and generate transcripts". kernel/roads_gcp.py, kernel/roads_gcp_config.py, kernel/roads_gcp_check.py, kernel/roads_gcp_ops.py, kernel/road_settings.py (`rihmasto road`), cockpit/road_routes.py, cockpit/static/roads.js, docs/guides/gcp.md. Rendered, validated and tested against a fake gcloud on PATH; not yet run against a real Google Cloud project.

acceptance.given: a gcp-cloudrun road entry, whole or with a gap (no deploying identity, a project id or region Cloud Run does not take, no repository, a cron or time zone Cloud Scheduler does not take, a secret given a value or not in Secret Manager, egress none without the VPC)
acceptance.when: IT configures it in the cockpit or with rihmasto road configure, or chooses a project's workload and schedule
acceptance.then: a whole entry is written to paved_roads.json and the factory's ledger records who configured it with the entry's sha256; each gap is named and nothing is written; only a named person with the it persona sets a road or a project's road, workload and schedule, and the choice is recorded

acceptance.given: a configured road and a release, as a service and as a scheduled job
acceptance.when: its deploy package is made for the test environment and for production
acceptance.then: the package holds a serving.knative.dev/v1 Service (one instance, port 8080, /health probes, the runtime service account, the image pinned by digest, settings by value and secrets as Secret Manager references, never PORT) or a run.googleapis.com/v1 Job with a Cloud Scheduler job that calls it in production only, and the exact gcloud commands with the environment's project, the region and the deploying identity; the YAML reads back as the model, and a rendering edited, stale or holding a secret that is not a Secret Manager reference fails validation

acceptance.given: a product at production maturity on the road and a fake gcloud on PATH
acceptance.when: it is delivered, and a person and IT decide its cards
acceptance.then: it is built by Cloud Build and deployed to the test project first: a service answers /health with the release's version, a job is executed once and its execution decides the smoke check, and a failing execution stops the release before the deploy gate; nothing reaches the production project until IT approves the deploy gate, after which a service runs as a candidate and is promoted and a job gets its image and its Cloud Scheduler job

acceptance.given: a second release on the road
acceptance.when: it is promoted, and IT or operations rolls it back with a reason
acceptance.then: a service's candidate revision takes no traffic beside the current one until promotion moves all of it, and the rollback moves the traffic back to the previous revision; a job keeps its previous image and the rollback gives it back; anyone else is refused, and the rollback is recorded with who, why and how

acceptance.given: a scheduled job running in production

acceptance.then: the probe records the last executions, passes when the latest finished one succeeded, is not measured while none has finished, and fails when it failed, which opens an incident card the relay notifies

acceptance.given: a road with no gcloud on PATH, gcloud not signed in, or an incomplete entry
acceptance.when: a release is delivered, or rihmasto road list and road render are asked
acceptance.then: a road card names exactly what is missing and nothing is built or deployed; the commands say the same and render the YAML and gcloud commands without running them

acceptance.then: Settings lists every paved road with what is missing and lets IT configure a Google Cloud road whose configuration is signed and recorded; the Releases view shows where each environment deploys and lets IT choose the road and the schedule; no console error, failed request or overflow

requirements.statement: A capability Rihmasto builds can read from and write to a Google Drive folder through the paved road's client, declared as a gdrive integration: it lists only the files that arrived since a cursor across every page, downloads a file and uploads a result, with its scopes stated and its credentials by name only (an OAuth token or a service account key file for a local run, the runtime service account on Google Cloud), and it never logs a token or a file's content.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24), on an adopted project, an agentic workflow that transcribes recordings: it must be "taken into the company's Google Cloud, to be run regularly, to read recordings in Google Drive and generate transcripts". kernel/connectors_gdrive.py (copied into the product as app/gdrive.py), kernel/gdrive_standin.py (the gate's and the tests' Drive v3 stand-in), kernel/integration_decl.py, kernel/integration_standins.py, kernel/compile.py, cockpit/static/roads.js, docs/guides/gcp.md.

acceptance.given: a Drive folder with recordings, other files, a subfolder and a trashed file, and a cursor

acceptance.then: every page is read, the folder's files come oldest first, a second run returns nothing, a file that arrives in the cursor's own second or later is returned once, and an id or cursor that is not one is refused before any request

acceptance.given: an integration declared read-write, and one declared read
acceptance.when: the client downloads a file, uploads a transcript and keeps its cursor in the folder
acceptance.then: the bytes and the uploaded file are as sent, a file is found by name so a rerun writes nothing twice, the cursor is updated in place; an integration declared read refuses to upload before any request, and a token with the read scope is refused by Drive

acceptance.given: a token by name, a service account's key file, or no credential on Google Cloud
acceptance.when: the client calls Drive, and Drive refuses or fails
acceptance.then: a token variable is used as given, a key file's JWT signed with RS256 is exchanged for the declared scopes, the metadata server is asked for the Drive scopes; a refusal names the call and the status and never the token or the content, a 5xx is retried, and nothing is printed or logged

acceptance.given: a spec that declares a gdrive integration
acceptance.when: it is compiled, the gate runs the product's tests, and the integration is bound on a Google Cloud road
acceptance.then: the spec's guidance and kinds name Google Drive, the kernel writes its INT- requirement, the product gets app/gdrive.py importable with nothing from Rihmasto, the gate's Drive stand-in serves the tests and catches a write to a read integration, and the deploy package names the Drive settings and the credential as a Secret Manager reference, never a value

acceptance.given: the cockpit in a browser
acceptance.when: a person opens Settings
acceptance.then: the Integrations card shows the Google Drive connector with its scopes, its credentials by name and the client the product imports, in the dark and the light theme, wide and narrow, with no console error

requirements.statement: A person reviews what agents and automations did since they last looked, across their projects or one project, from the records alone, grouped and ranked by what needs them (waiting on you, went wrong, decided for you, shipped, from your IDE, cost and usage), each item linked to its record and saying who or what did it; they act in place through the existing signed routes, mark what they looked at as reviewed, mark the whole review done, and can get it every morning as a message.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24), quoting an engineer: "You're not supposed to watch Claude Code work. You're supposed to wake up and review what it shipped." And: "so how can Rihmasto be for reviewing all visible work of agents, essentially". kernel/review.py, kernel/review_items.py, kernel/review_ledger.py, kernel/review_marks.py, kernel/review_digest.py, kernel/review_cli.py; cockpit/review_routes.py and cockpit/static/review.js; docs/guides/review.md.

acceptance.given: a home where builder cells merged one task and failed another's gate, which escalated, a model endpoint failed, a release went to a test environment, a model run was priced, an autopilot assumed answers by its delegation in a person's name, the factory assumed answers with due dates, a commit was gated from a developer's IDE and a cockpit job failed

acceptance.then: the items are grouped as waiting on you (the cards the persona may decide, with their age and verdicts), went wrong, decided for you (overturnable, each assumption once), shipped (the merged task with its gate verdict, rounds and diff stats, the release to test), from your IDE (verdict, who asked and the diff) and cost by project and role; each group is ranked, every item names who or what did it and links only to views the cockpit routes and to its own ledger record, and reading records nothing

acceptance.given: a person who has never marked a review done, and another person
acceptance.when: the first marks their review done, more happens, and one project's review is marked done
acceptance.then: a first review covers the last 24 hours; review_done records the period and each group's count, and the person's next review starts there with nothing shown twice, while the other person's still covers the last 24 hours; a project's marker moves that project's review only; a period asked for overrides the marker

acceptance.given: a review with a shipped task, an escalation card, a factory assumption and a delegated decision
acceptance.when: the person marks the task reviewed, approves the card, overturns the assumption and the delegated decision, stops the delegation and reports a change from the review
acceptance.then: each goes through its own signed route and is recorded with the person and persona; review_marked records the item and its revision and the review shows who looked; a write by a non-person, a card marked instead of decided, or an item that did not happen is refused and records nothing; the preview drawer reads the diff file by file

acceptance.given: a review in the cockpit
acceptance.when: the person presses Mark all reviewed, across their projects or on one project
acceptance.then: review_done is recorded with the counts in the factory's ledger or that project's, signed, and the review now starts at the person's last review

acceptance.given: a person's morning digest at 07:30 local on weekdays to a receiver IT configured for their persona, on 127.0.0.1
acceptance.when: relay rounds run before and after that time, again the same day, the next day with nothing new, and on a Saturday
acceptance.then: the digest goes once per local day after its time, with the review's headline, its groups' first items, a project bound to an autopilot's sandbox left out and counted, and one link to the Review page; it is held back when nothing happened and the delivery log says so; it is never sent on a day it is not set for; a mail receiver gets the same

requirements.statement: Insights show health, compliance, governance, security, context drift, QA and token, skill and memory usage of the projects and their agentic features, per project and factory-wide, over 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days or all records: stat tiles and charts with a one-line insight computed by rule, every number counted from the records and none estimated, "not measured" with why and how where there is no record, and an export as JSON, CSV or OpenTelemetry-style JSON for the customer's own observability tools that sends nothing anywhere (D-0017).
requirements.notes: The owner, 2026-11-24: "about the insights view, inspired by the different dimensions of Rihmasto + Gnomon + an agentic observability stack: enable data visualization views, dashboards and insights on health, compliance, governance, security, context drift, QA, token/skill/memory usage of projects and their agentic features." kernel/insights/ (the read models, the rule-based lines, the export and the command line), cockpit/insights_routes.py, cockpit/static/insights.js and insights.css; docs/guides/insights.md.

acceptance.when: each dimension is read for the factory and for one project over 24h, 7d, 30d and all
acceptance.then: every figure equals what the records hold for that window: tokens and cost summed per project, role, model, endpoint, runner and local or hosted, tool calls by tool from the trails, skills used and compactions from the audit kinds, gate pass rate and rounds per task, decisions and time to decide, open findings and secrets; a tile compares with the window before it

acceptance.when: it is read, exported or drawn
acceptance.then: it is not measured: its value is empty, never 0, and it says why and how to get it measured; the export gives it no data point and an empty CSV value, and what a dimension cannot measure here is listed with why and how

acceptance.given: figures for a window and the window before it

acceptance.then: each tile and chart has one plain line computed by rule from its own figures: a change against the window before (doubled, grew n-fold, rose, fell, halved, held steady) with both numbers, the largest of a ranked list with its share, the tasks that needed many rounds, the oldest card waiting; a figure not measured says why

acceptance.given: a project whose spec was written before merges, whose requirements lack passing criteria, whose canon holds a contradiction and whose runs trimmed their context, and whose ledger chain is intact or broken
acceptance.when: context drift and governance are read
acceptance.then: drift counts the merges since the spec, the requirements without a verified or held-out criterion, the contradictions, the assumptions settled against open and the runs that trimmed their context or came near their window; governance counts decisions by person, delegation or automation and says which ledgers verify

acceptance.given: the same home
acceptance.when: rihmasto insights runs with and without a project, a dimension, a window and --json, and rihmasto insights export runs with --format json, csv and otlp-json, to a file and to the terminal
acceptance.then: the text says each figure, its line and how to measure what is not measured; the JSON is the read model; the CSV has one row per figure; the OTLP JSON has one gauge per measured tile and one span per model run with gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens and gen_ai.usage.output_tokens; nothing opens a network connection

acceptance.given: the cockpit in headless Chrome over that home
acceptance.when: a person opens Insights from the sidebar, switches every dimension, the window and the scope, toggles a chart to its table, opens a project's Insights tab, pins a tile to Home and exports, in dark and light at 1440 and 390 pixels
acceptance.then: every dimension renders its tiles and charts or says not measured, nothing scrolls sideways, every control is named, the chart colours pass the palette validator in both themes, the pinned tile shows on Home, and no console error, failed request or Content-Security-Policy violation happens

acceptance.then: the map leads to Insights, its controls say where they are, and the snapshot carries a few key figures per dimension with no project title, no insight line and no decision's reason; with a project open only that project's figures

acceptance.then: the checks are measured from each enabled check's last check_ran result (failing counted, not measured said apart) and the repository drift from alignment_scanned, with the alignment_accepted and alignment_rejected decisions; neither says not measured once its records exist

acceptance.then: each run is recorded in the project's ledger as model_run with its role, model, endpoint, tokens, cost when priced (not measured otherwise), duration and task, never the prompt or the holdouts; the builder keeps its own gnomon_run; Insights' usage counts every role; the refused build is recorded as autonomy_capped and Governance counts it

acceptance.when: Insights' governance and usage are read
acceptance.then: Governance counts the agents' proposals and how they were settled; Usage counts Rihma's channel answers (model_run with task channel) and their tokens, or says the tokens were not recorded

requirements.statement: Rihmasto captures the development structure a team keeps in its own repository (specs and requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, decisions, API contracts, test suites, task lists, CI/CD, quality tools, architecture documents and the AI tools' setup, in the conventions IDE tools use), proposes how it maps onto the project (requirements, criteria, a trace from the existing tests with its basis and confidence, tasks, decisions, API contract references, and the gaps), lets a person accept, edit or reject each proposal, writes what is accepted into the project's contract and records signed by that person, suggests changes for the repository as text or a patch without ever writing there, shows the drift after the repository changes, and gives the accepted contract and the open gaps to the IDE so the work can continue there.
requirements.notes: The owner, 2026-11-24: "I've been working on something in Claude Code or Cursor or any IDE (VS Code, Antigravity and so on). They have their own contracts and specs and tests and everything code-structure-wise. Rihmasto's job is to capture all that structure and context, and suggest how it would be configured the Rihmasto way. There should be a view of suggested changes, suggested alignment. It has to capture any existing repo structure and feed it so the work can be continued or further developed, not necessarily in Rihmasto: in an IDE, because many people prefer that." kernel/repo_structure.py, kernel/repo_specs.py, kernel/repo_suites.py, kernel/alignment.py, kernel/alignment_suggest.py, kernel/alignment_records.py, kernel/alignment_contract.py, kernel/alignment_cli.py, cockpit/align_routes.py, cockpit/static/alignment.js, docs/guides/alignment.md.

acceptance.given: a repository kept with spec-kit, Kiro, ADR, Gherkin, OpenAPI, pytest, jest and GitHub Actions conventions, with a file that holds a secret and files that would leave a mark if anything ran them
acceptance.when: its structure is captured from a folder and from a committed revision
acceptance.then: the structure map names each convention and where it is: requirements with their own refs and their criteria, tasks done or open, decisions with their status, the API contract's operations, each test's name and framework, how the tests are run, the CI jobs and whether they run tests, the quality tools and the AI tools' files, with commit dates when there is a history; the secret is not read and never shown, and nothing found is run

acceptance.given: the structure map of that repository
acceptance.when: alignment proposes how it maps onto the project
acceptance.then: requirements keep their own refs and titles as their source with a proposed Rihmasto id, criteria are given / when / then from acceptance scenarios, EARS and Gherkin (derived from the statement, and said so, when the repository gives none), each test is traced to a criterion by name, by file or by text similarity with its basis and confidence, tasks carry done or open and the requirements they serve, ADRs become decisions and API contracts references, every item says what it adds to the project, why and its source lines, and the same source gives the same item ids

acceptance.given: a repository whose spec is older than the code it describes, with a criterion no test can observe, a test with no requirement, requirements with no test and a CI that runs no test
acceptance.when: it is aligned
acceptance.then: each gap is an item with its reason, the summary counts the tests that trace to a criterion and the requirements with no test, the suggested changes for the repository are text to copy or a patch that git apply takes, and nothing in the repository changes

acceptance.given: an attached project aligned with its repository
acceptance.when: a person accepts, edits and rejects items, a group at once too, and a non-person, a rejection of what the contract holds, an id another requirement has and an edit of a field the item does not have are tried
acceptance.then: accepted requirements and criteria are in the project's contract, customer-endorsed by that person with a note naming the repository source, and the contract passes its check; tasks, decisions and traces are kept as the project's records; the ledger holds alignment_accepted and alignment_rejected with the item ids, the person and the persona; each refusal writes nothing

acceptance.given: an aligned project whose repository then changes: a requirement added, an accepted criterion restated, a feature removed
acceptance.when: the repository is read again
acceptance.then: the drift lists the new, changed and removed items; the restated criterion reads changed since accepted until a person accepts it again, which restates it in the contract; unchanged items keep their ids and decisions

acceptance.given: an aligned project
acceptance.when: rihmasto structure, rihmasto align (show, --scan, --drift, accept, edit, reject) and the cockpit's alignment routes are used
acceptance.then: they show and record the same, a write with no person is refused (exit 2, 403) and writes nothing, the text for the IDE lists the requirements accepted from the repository and the gaps still open, and the repo gate's note names the accepted criteria a change's tests touch

acceptance.given: an adopted project
acceptance.when: it is aligned and a requirement accepted
acceptance.then: the repository read is the upstream as last fetched, the requirement is in the project's spec and the contract is compiled again with every other task keeping its id and committed to the mirror's main, and the imported requirement's task is held as the existing work, never built by the factory

acceptance.given: an attached repository in the cockpit
acceptance.when: a person follows the offer on the Overview to the Alignment tab, reads the repository, accepts, edits, rejects, accepts a group at once and copies and downloads a suggested change, in dark and light at 1440 and 390 pixels
acceptance.then: each step shows its result and is recorded with that person, every control has an accessible name, nothing scrolls sideways, no console error, failed request or Content-Security-Policy violation happens, and the repository is never written

acceptance.then: it carries the requirements accepted from the repository and the open gaps, inside its markers; before any scan it carries neither

acceptance.given: an attached project scanned once, and an automation from the template "Re-read the repository for alignment when it changes" (a repo trigger and the align_scan action)
acceptance.when: the repository gets a new commit and the scheduler ticks after its poll interval
acceptance.then: the repository is read again for alignment, signed by the automation's owner; alignment_scanned records the drift since the scan before (new, changed and removed items), the automation's history says what drifted, and Insights' repository drift counts it

requirements.statement: A person with a persona the project's console allows (developer and IT unless IT changes it) runs commands, or asks Gnomon, in a project's workspace from the cockpit's Console tab or the command line, sees the output line by line as it comes, can stop it and is stopped at a time limit; every run is a job recorded in the project's ledger as console_ran (who, persona, command line, exit, duration, never an environment value or the output), goes through IT's isolation runner while access is enforced, and a person at the cockpit's own machine can open the operating system's terminal in the workspace (refused through a public origin); the person keeps developing in their own IDE.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24): "where do we draw the line if a user wants to run a Gnomon shell inside Rihmasto? Could they develop or do something to some extent inside Rihmasto? In maintenance and administration you want automations of compliance checks or integration CI/CD checks or whatsoever, because eventually it is not just about getting something deployed, but how you keep on monitoring it and governing it and having checks. It should be effortless that if a user wants to run some of these things, it is possible inside Rihmasto, while they keep developing in their chosen IDE. And if they want to run something inside a terminal in Rihmasto, it should be possible." kernel/console.py, kernel/console_run.py, kernel/console_offers.py, kernel/console_term.py, kernel/console_cli.py, cockpit/console_routes.py, cockpit/static/console.js, docs/guides/console-and-checks.md (where the line is between your IDE, the console and a real terminal).

acceptance.then: an attached repository runs in its own folder, a built project in the console's working copy made at the first run whose origin cannot push, a project without code is refused with why; the offers are the stated commands, the test command detected by rule, package.json scripts, Makefile targets and CI steps, a step that needs the shell marked so

acceptance.then: its first line is readable before it ends (the log read by offset gives whole lines while it runs), stdin is closed so nothing waits for keys, one program runs without a shell, and a line with a pipe or && is refused unless the person asks for the shell

acceptance.when: its time limit runs out, or a person presses Stop
acceptance.then: the command and every process it started are stopped, the log and console_ran say timed_out or stopped, and the child never finishes its work

acceptance.when: a console run or a Gnomon run is asked for
acceptance.then: without a runner it is refused before anything runs or is recorded; with one the command runs in the container with no network, no capabilities, a read-only root and the workspace at /work, and a Gnomon run goes through IT's cells command

acceptance.then: gnomon task runs in the workspace under its own surface with the person's words, the role when given and --yes only when asked, recorded as kind gnomon; a person's repository without a surface is refused and never written to; the confidential project's run is refused

acceptance.given: the cockpit on 127.0.0.1 with a terminal launcher, and the same cockpit behind a public origin

Each journey names ordered steps, why they matter, their real button and command, prerequisites and recovery; each step is measured from the project's or factory's records, so Ask Rihma, the Overview, the command line and walkthroughs agree on the next step. A person can keep a signed, per-person guided panel across views and reloads, do a step through its existing route, mark or skip it, and stop without undoing their work. Journey questions are answered by rule without a model, and other how-to questions ground the model in the same steps.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25), after asking how to start a brownfield project: the answer only described the project view instead of saying to run the assessment, and asked why the user could not request hand-holding to feed in an existing project. kernel/journeys.py holds the catalogue; kernel/journey_state.py measures it; kernel/journey_guide.py keeps the guide; kernel/journey_chat.py and kernel/journey_intent.py answer and ground Ask Rihma; kernel/journey_cli.py, cockpit/journey_routes.py and cockpit/static/journey.js expose it. Rihmasto's own scheduler, not Gnomon loops: an automation is signed, checked against the access file before every run, reacts to ledger events and webhooks and records every run in the ledger (the guide says why).
