requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24): "What Gnomon enables as engine is harness agnosticism, to be a governance glue inside Rihmasto, among many other features like compliance, security etc." D-0019 (other harnesses run the factory's cells, opt-in, the evidence saying so), amending D-0003 and D-0015. kernel/runners/ (the runner interface, detection, the governance glue, the docker sandbox, choices on IT cards, the CLI), kernel/dispatch.py, kernel/evidence_pack.py, cockpit/runner_routes.py, cockpit/static/runners.js, docs/guides/harnesses.md. Every harness in the tests is a fake executable written by the test.

acceptance.given: a machine with some harnesses installed and some not
acceptance.when: a person checks the runners (`rihmasto runners check`, or Check in Settings > Runners)
acceptance.then: each runner is found with its version, and one that is not found says so, where it was looked for and what to do; each harness is started headless with a mode that never prompts and its tools held to the working copy (claude -p with stream-json and dontAsk, codex exec --json with its workspace-write sandbox, opencode run --format json, a named command with {prompt_file} and {workdir} filled in)

acceptance.given: a project whose builder runner IT approved (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or a named command)
acceptance.when: a task is built
acceptance.then: the harness gets the task's envelope with its write scope, its protected paths, the criteria whose tests must fail first and the project's own conventions (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, rules files); its diff is judged at one revision by the gate's signals with the write-scope and custody checks beside them; a warranted change merges; and the round's record names the runner, its version, its tool calls, what it changed and the assurance "checked after the run"

acceptance.given: a harness that touches a protected path, writes outside the task's write scope, or writes a test that cannot fail
acceptance.when: its round is judged
acceptance.then: the verdict is a violation (or failed) with the reason as an objection, nothing reaches main, the verifier does not run over a changed protected path, and after its repair rounds the task escalates

acceptance.given: holdout scenarios in their custody and the factory's home and lanes named in the environment
acceptance.when: a harness runs a builder round
acceptance.then: neither the working copy, nor the task it is given, nor the environment it runs in holds or names the custody; a working copy that held a custody file, or overlapped the custody, is a violation

acceptance.given: a person who chooses a runner other than Gnomon
acceptance.when: they save the choice, and IT decides it
acceptance.then: a runner card opens that only IT may decide, with the version found on this machine pinned, and the runner applies only from IT's approval; a version other than the pinned one, a runner not found, or the docker sandbox where Docker does not answer refuses the task before any round runs, with the reason in the ledger; going back to Gnomon applies at once; a non-person or a persona that may not choose writes nothing

acceptance.given: a factory default, a project's own choice and a choice per role
acceptance.when: a task is built
acceptance.then: the builder and the verifier may run on different runners, a project's choice wins over the factory's, a choice that gives the verifier the builder's model family is refused, and a harness verifier reviews a throwaway copy of the lane, read-only, its answer being the verifier signal

acceptance.given: rounds run by Gnomon and by other harnesses
acceptance.when: an evidence pack is exported
acceptance.then: cell-runners.json lists each round's runner, version and assurance, the README says how many rounds had in-run policy enforced by Gnomon and how many were checked after the run and by which harness, and a round another harness ran is never shown as Gnomon-level assurance, whatever its own record says

acceptance.given: a choice with the docker sandbox
acceptance.when: its harness runs
acceptance.then: the container mounts only the working copy, drops every capability, takes no new privileges, gets keys by variable name only, and has no network or an internal network whose one way out is a proxy that tunnels only to the model endpoint and refuses any other host

acceptance.given: the command line, and a factory with no runner chosen
acceptance.when: a person runs `rihmasto runners list|check|set`, and a task is built
acceptance.then: list, check and set work, set is signed and refused for a non-person or a family clash; with no choice Gnomon builds exactly as before and the round says in-run policy enforced by Gnomon; a write scope is read as the task names it (** crosses folders, * does not)

acceptance.given: the cockpit, dark and light, at 1440 and 390 px
acceptance.when: a developer opens Settings > Runners, checks this machine, chooses a runner, IT approves it on the page, and Project settings is opened
acceptance.then: each step works with no console error, failed request or CSP violation, every control has a name and nothing is wider than the screen; the role shows the runner, its pinned version and "Checked after the run", never Gnomon's in-run words; Project settings shows the project's builder and verifier with their assurance and links to the page

acceptance.given: a project whose working copy holds AGENTS.md and a Cursor rule whose globs match only web files, and a harness other than Gnomon chosen for its builder
acceptance.when: a task whose write scope is the Python files is built by that harness, and an adopted project's task is built by it too
acceptance.then: the harness is given the instructions that apply to the files the task may write, recognised and matched as a Gnomon builder's envelope matches them (kernel/agent_context_use.py): AGENTS.md and not the web rule; an adopted project's envelope, which already holds that section, is not given it twice

acceptance.given: a confidential project whose builder IT approved to run with Claude Code (its own hosted endpoint), or with a harness outside the docker sandbox
acceptance.when: the project is built
acceptance.then: the build is refused as a hosted role is: `confidential_refused` names the role, the runner and the host, no cell runs and nothing is sent; the same harness in the docker sandbox reaching only a local endpoint is not refused

acceptance.given: a runner chosen for a project and waiting on IT's card, and a project waiting on its look at the spec
acceptance.when: What's next and the Inbox are read
acceptance.then: What's next names the runner card with who decides it (IT) and opens Settings > Runners for that project, and the go-ahead's Go and Skip; the factory's Inbox and the Inbox across projects hold the runner card for IT, grouped with the cards a deploy waits on

requirements.statement: Real projects of every shape feed in as a person would feed them through New project: housekeeping and archives are read by rule, uncommitted work, workspaces, copies and projects adopted already are said with their choices, long scans show progress and refusals what to do, a confidential adoption is said plainly with a one-click fix, and an adopted project is held as what it is: its kind of work, its real state, its health, its areas and its watch.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24): "I will give you examples to scan and hook into Rihmasto (do it like you would in the UI to understand how feeding in projects works). Here are very different ones: a machine learning / fine-tuning experiment, a transcript agent to be productionised, another software factory product for a customer to monitor, govern and develop further, my local devbrain project as a second brain of my dev and agentic work, and my massive game dev project, to monitor further development, get ideas to optimise or improve it, and monitor how developing assets, the game world, lore etc. goes." Kernel: kernel/material.py, kernel/material_kinds.py, kernel/material_zip.py, kernel/material_git.py, kernel/source_guard.py, kernel/profiles_shapes.py, kernel/adopt.py, kernel/adopt_seen.py, kernel/adopt_stated.py, kernel/adopt_watch.py, kernel/adopted_state.py, kernel/areas.py, kernel/confidential_local.py, kernel/status.py, kernel/track.py, kernel/assistant_status.py; cockpit/source_routes.py, cockpit/adopted_routes.py, cockpit/static/scan.js, cockpit/static/feedin.js, cockpit/static/adopted.js, cockpit/static/folders.js. Docs: docs/guides/inputs.md, docs/brownfield.md, docs/guides/profiles.md.

acceptance.given: a folder whose top holds a README and many housekeeping files (.gitattributes, .gitignore, .editorconfig, .ignore, a nested .gitignore, SHA256SUMS and checksum files, .env.example, lockfiles)
acceptance.when: it is scanned
acceptance.then: the housekeeping files are listed and counted under housekeeping, never read in full as material, and the root README is read first and in full before plans and other documents

acceptance.given: a folder holding a zip archive of results (csv, json, md, txt, html, logs, images, an archive inside it, a secret-looking entry)
acceptance.when: it is scanned
acceptance.then: the archive's entries are listed and its readable text is read from inside it by the same rules and within the budget, never extracted to disk; an entry over the size cap is listed, an archive or entry that inflates beyond the ratio or total caps is refused as a zip bomb, and an archive inside an archive is listed, not opened

acceptance.given: a git repository with uncommitted changes and untracked files
acceptance.when: it is scanned and adopted
acceptance.then: the scan and the dialog say how many uncommitted changes and untracked files are not in the last commit and that they will not be included, offer adopting the last commit (the default) or the working copy as it is now (a snapshot baseline, the folder unchanged), and the preview scans exactly what will be adopted, so its numbers are the adoption's

acceptance.given: a folder or repository that is already adopted (the same resolved path or the same origin, credentials taken out)
acceptance.when: it is given to New project again
acceptance.then: the dialog says it is already adopted with Open <project>, and adopting it again as a new project needs the explicit Adopt it again as a new project (the adopt route refuses it otherwise)

acceptance.given: a confidential adoption while some roles' models are hosted
acceptance.when: the folder is scanned
acceptance.then: the dialog says Adopting works (it calls no model) and names the roles that would be refused until they use a local model, never saying refused for a step that proceeds; when a local or private endpoint is in the routing, Use my local model for these roles points them at it in one click, signed and recorded as a Models setup change, keeping the verifier to another family than the builder's

acceptance.given: a folder holding several git repositories and copies of one (_snapshot, -copy, -experiment, -prep)
acceptance.when: it is scanned
acceptance.then: the dialog lists the repositories with their commits and uncommitted counts and offers Adopt each as its own project (choosing which) or Adopt the folder as one; a file whose text another holds is read once and listed as its copy, so a copy does not eat the budget

acceptance.given: a long scan, a refused folder or a scan that fails
acceptance.when: a person scans it in New project
acceptance.then: the scan shows its progress (files looked at, the time and the folder) and can be cancelled, and a refusal or an error is shown in the scan step with what to do, never a scan that stays on Scanning the folder

acceptance.given: a folder outside the home and the configured roots
acceptance.when: it is refused
acceptance.then: the refusal offers Allow <folder> to a single operator (after a yes) or says Ask IT to allow it under enforced access; a folder allowed in Settings (stored in the factory home, signed and recorded) is read at once, without a restart; system folders, folders of keys and a drive's root are never allowed

acceptance.given: a project shaped like a game, an ML experiment or model, a knowledge or tooling project, a library or CLI, or a data pipeline
acceptance.when: its kind of work is proposed
acceptance.then: each has a work profile with its panel focus, questions and gates, recognised by rule from its words and from its files (a game engine's project files, assets beside lore and world documents; training scripts, datasets and evaluation results; a notes vault; DAGs and dbt), the Which kind of work question offers them, and the header shows Kind: not chosen yet while no kind is chosen

acceptance.given: an adopted project
acceptance.when: its page is opened
acceptance.then: it shows its real state (adopted: monitoring, maintaining or improving; what was taken; its baseline and the command that produced it; its activity) instead of the seven stages ticked by the adoption, and its maturity is asked in the dialog (How is it used today: an experiment, a prototype, in use by a few, in production), inferred by rule from its files, never defaulted to demo

acceptance.given: an adopted project whose existing tests fail at the baseline
acceptance.when: its health is read
acceptance.then: existing tests fail at the baseline (recorded, not judged) is a health item and a Track reason, never On track

acceptance.given: an adopted project whose instructions state a test command that no known runner maps (a script of its own)
acceptance.when: a person runs it as the baseline
acceptance.then: it is offered on the project page and run only after the person's yes (it runs the project's own code; through the isolation runner under enforced access), only as stated, and the baseline records which command produced it and who said yes

acceptance.given: a project adopted to monitor or maintain
acceptance.when: a person sets up the watch it offers
acceptance.then: new commits upstream become a summary in Review and the timeline, the activity by area is summed up weekly and failed checks notify a channel, through the automations engine in that person's name (else the upstream polling), and the project says Watching: ...

acceptance.given: an adopted repository that is not just code (a game, content, data, ML)
acceptance.when: it is adopted or watched
acceptance.then: an inventory by top-level area (files, types, sizes, asset kinds such as models, textures, audio and scenes), activity from its git history (commits, files changed and lines per area over 7 and 30 days, recently active areas, authors) and an index of design, lore and world documents by title are kept, shown as an Areas card, served to Insights and answered by Ask Rihma (how are the assets coming along?)

acceptance.given: a folder of documents only
acceptance.when: it is scanned in New project
acceptance.then: the dialog offers Build something from these documents (a new project, as before) or Track and evaluate this work: a project in a monitoring state whose material is the documents, with no build questions, and the ML experiment profile when its files fit

acceptance.given: a person in the cockpit in a real browser, light and dark, 1440 and 390 px wide
acceptance.when: they feed in neutral folders of every shape through New project (a documents-only experiment with a results zip, a repository with uncommitted work and skills, a workspace with a copy, a long scan, a folder outside the allowed ones, a game-like repository adopted already) and open the adopted project's page
acceptance.then: the warnings, offers and adoptions are as above, the page shows the kind, the adopted state, the failed baseline as health, the Areas card and the watch; nothing scrolls sideways and there is no console error, failed request or CSP violation

acceptance.given: an adopted project (a documents-only experiment among them) that a person works on
acceptance.when: they take a hand-off brief, ask Rihma how to work on it in their terminal or with a goal to compare or evaluate runs, give the Plug in walkthrough the same folder, and open its page and tasks
acceptance.then: the brief names the command its baseline ran or says no test command is known (never the paved road's suite) and its insights in plain words; Ask Rihma answers with the project's own id and the person's name in each command and Take me there to the Console, and a goal to compare or evaluate runs gets a plan (a change, the evaluation as a check, the watch, a hand-off); the walkthrough says it is already adopted with Open the project before any other question, and offers Track and evaluate this work for documents only; the page names who adopted it as requested by, and the adopted task says it was adopted as it was, never Not built yet

acceptance.given: a confidential project scanned in New project while the analyst role's endpoint is hosted, with a person named in Requested by
acceptance.when: the scan's summary is shown, the person takes the one-click local model, and the project is adopted
acceptance.then: the summary says the characters would go only to a local model and that the hosted endpoint is refused, never that they would be sent to it (said again when Confidential is ticked or unticked); the one-click choice is signed by the dialog's Requested by without the person menu; and the adopted project records who requested it

acceptance.given: an adopted project and a person who works on it from their own terminal
acceptance.when: they open its Console, Open a terminal here, or ask Ask Rihma how to work on it in their terminal
acceptance.then: the console offers the test command adoption's baseline ran before its working copy exists; the terminal has the rihmasto command on PATH (a shim in the factory home when Rihmasto is not installed); Ask Rihma answers with the real project id, the workspace open and submit commands, the baseline's test command and how to run rihmasto when it is not installed, with Take me there to Open a terminal here; a command the map gives names the project asked about, and the cockpit fills in the person's name

acceptance.given: an adopted project and a goal that names a cloud and a data source (to Google Cloud so it reads recordings from Google Drive)
acceptance.when: Ask Rihma plans it by rule
acceptance.then: the plan holds both goals: where it runs, with the Google Cloud road kind named, and the Drive integration; a confidential project is never offered a coding agent's hosted subscription for its model roles

acceptance.given: an adopted project handed off to a coding agent
acceptance.when: the hand-off brief is built
acceptance.then: How to run the tests gives the project's own suite as adoption's baseline ran it (never the paved road's unittest default), and the conventions name the project's own instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md)

acceptance.given: the walkthrough Plug in an existing project
acceptance.when: a person names a git repository with uncommitted work that is adopted already
acceptance.then: the scan is of its last commit (what is adopted) and says the uncommitted work, and the walkthrough says Already adopted as its title with Open the project, Adopt it again as a new project (only then is it adopted again) and Give another folder

acceptance.given: a confidential project adopted while the only hosted role is the verifier and every local model in use is of the builder's family
acceptance.when: the New project dialog says what a confidential adoption means, and the project's page is opened
acceptance.then: the dialog says why there is no one-click local model (the verifier needs a local model of another family than the builder's, naming the family and the local models in use) instead of only pointing at Models setup, and the project's header says Confidential: local models only

acceptance.given: an adopted project whose test suite is found by rule, handed off and given a goal
acceptance.when: the console offers its commands, the hand-off brief is built and Ask Rihma plans a goal said as Help me reach this goal: ...
acceptance.then: the suite's button reads Run the tests (<runner>), never a label that reads as another command; the brief's insights are words with the figures not measured left out, never a data structure; and the plan quotes the goal without its lead-in

acceptance.given: an adopted project open in the cockpit, and Ask Rihma asked questions that name the command line, the IDE, the tests or the commands
acceptance.when: a question asks how to work on the project itself (in a terminal, an IDE, or editing its code myself, from the project or from Home naming its title), where to set up the IDE, how to run its tests or evaluation, or where to state its commands, and others only name the command line, a shell or a CLI
acceptance.then: working on the project itself gets its workspace, shell and IDE commands with the person's name and how they run on this machine (python -m kernel.cli --home when rihmasto is not installed or the home is another); the IDE, tests and commands questions get their own answer (Work on it from your IDE, the test commands or where to name one, Console settings); a question that only names the command line (export the evidence pack, approve the plan, enable a check, the console's shell option, add a CLI to my product, develop monitoring, work on the alignment items, what the agents work on) is not given the terminal recipe

acceptance.given: an adopted project, and goals said as fix the crash in the deploy command, fix the bug in the login page, and add an option and deploy it to production
acceptance.when: Ask Rihma plans each goal
acceptance.then: a fix is a goal planned as development (build it in a branch of your own), never an output such as a web app with sign-in, and building comes before delivering through the deploy gate

acceptance.given: a confidential project handed off to an agent, and a brief for one change C-0001 nobody has decided yet
acceptance.when: the hand-off brief and Ask Rihma's Hand it to a coding agent step are built
acceptance.then: the brief and the step say Confidential: local models only (a hosted coding agent sends the repository to its host); the change's brief says it is not decided yet and who decides it, that it alone is the scope, and lists the project's other findings as context, not as feedback to address

acceptance.given: real repositories with a template command in AGENTS.md, a path that looks like a token, two clones of one origin, BMAD bullet requirements, GDScript, scratch tests in an output folder, top-level skills, a demo's specs and a confidential adoption's one-click fix
acceptance.when: they are read, offered and adopted
acceptance.then: a template command fills the command line instead of running and is labelled by its script; a path is not masked as a secret; the second clone of an origin is a copy, not ticked by default; a wrapped bullet requirement is read whole without its marker; GDScript is a language; errors while collecting are not failing tests and pytest skips generated output folders; skills/<name>/SKILL.md is an AI-tool file; unmeasured insights are left out of the brief; a demo's specs are not the product's requirements; and the local-model fix says it changes the routing for every project on the machine

acceptance.given: an adopted project worked on in a workspace, whose repository commits its own .mcp.json, and whose tests unittest's discovery does not find
acceptance.when: a workspace is opened, its work submitted through the gate, and the Console visited before its first run
acceptance.then: Rihma's MCP server is merged into the project's .mcp.json (its own servers kept) and never sent in the person's commits; the gate judges the submission by the project's own suite as its baseline ran it, passing when it fails no more tests than at the baseline; and the Console's first visit offers the commands found by rule in the repository's last commit

requirements.statement: A person with no API key can run Rihmasto's text roles (the analyst, the holdout author, the verifier and the assistant) with the coding agent they already have (Claude Code with their own login, Codex, OpenCode, or a command they name): the agent runs headless as a text completion with no tools in an empty folder, its answer, model, tokens and cost are read from its own output, and each call is recorded in the ledger as run by that harness, not through Gnomon's lane. The verifier stays another model family than the builder, a confidential project refuses a hosted harness, no harness is given the repository, the contract or the holdouts beyond what its role needs, and Models setup, Home and doctor offer the harness found on the machine.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24): "I would use this with Claude Code equivalently if OpenCode is not available. I should be able to virtually run it with any agentic harness with the help of Gnomon." Gnomon's endpoints are openai or ollama only, so the harness answers outside Gnomon's lane and the record says so (as D-0019); docs/upstream/gnomon-harness-provider.md proposes the Gnomon side. kernel/harness_model.py (the harness model and the guard in kernel/model.py run_gnomon_task), kernel/harness_setup.py (Models setup, `rihmasto models use`, doctor), hooks in kernel/lanes.py, kernel/confidential.py, kernel/models_setup.py, kernel/doctor.py and kernel/shape_cli.py, cockpit/shape_routes.py, cockpit/static/harness.js, docs/guides/harness-models.md. Every harness in the tests is a fake executable written by the test.

acceptance.given: Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode on this machine
acceptance.when: a role it answers is asked
acceptance.then: the harness is started headless as a text completion with no tools (claude -p --output-format json --tools "" with MCP servers and sessions off and the role's rules as the system prompt; codex exec --json in its read-only sandbox; opencode run --format json with every tool off and denied; a named command), in an empty temporary folder with the task on standard input or as a file; its answer, model, token use and cost are read from its own output, and a harness that fails or is not found says so

acceptance.given: the text roles answered by Claude Code (`rihmasto models use claude-code`)
acceptance.when: intake, the spec, Ask Rihma and a Shape it in chat answer run
acceptance.then: each runs through Claude Code, not Gnomon (the lane's surface keeps a placeholder endpoint nothing answers on), and each call is a model_run in the project's ledger (the factory's when no project) with the role, the harness, its version, the model, tokens, cost, duration and the assurance "run by Claude Code, not through Gnomon's lane: no Gnomon audit trail for this call"; the builder is never a harness model and a harness is never a fallback

acceptance.given: a builder and a verifier
acceptance.when: a harness is set for the verifier, or a verifier's harness answers
acceptance.then: a setting that makes the verifier the builder's model family is refused (Claude Code counts as claude, Codex as gpt, OpenCode and a command by the model or family named, which is required), and a verifier whose harness answered with the builder's family gives no verdict

acceptance.given: a confidential project
acceptance.when: its intake would run on Claude Code or Codex
acceptance.then: it is refused and recorded, nothing is sent, and Claude Code or Codex cannot be declared private; an OpenCode on a local model declared private serves it

acceptance.given: a project with holdout scenarios, and a change to review
acceptance.when: a harness answers a role
acceptance.then: its folder is empty and its environment names no factory home, lanes or keys; a task for any role but the holdout author that quotes a holdout scenario is refused before anything runs; the verifier is given the change's diff, never the repository or the contract

acceptance.given: Models setup
acceptance.when: a person looks at it, uses a harness and tests a role
acceptance.then: the harnesses on this machine are listed with their versions and presets Use Claude Code (your login), Use Codex and Use OpenCode; `rihmasto models use` and POST /api/models/use are signed by a person and recorded; a harness role reads ready without Gnomon or a key, and Test sends a tiny prompt through the harness and shows its latency or its error, recording nothing; the page says a harness is slower than an API and spends the person's subscription

acceptance.given: a machine with a coding agent and a missing key or no Gnomon
acceptance.when: `rihmasto doctor` runs
acceptance.then: it lists the harnesses found and suggests "No API key? Claude Code found: use it" with the command, until a text role uses one

acceptance.given: the cockpit in a browser with no key and Claude Code and Codex on the machine
acceptance.when: a person uses them from Home and Models setup
acceptance.then: Home's Set up a model card offers Use Claude Code with the version found and goes once it is used; Models setup shows which harness answers each role, tests one, and sets the verifier to Codex, in dark at 1440 px and light at 390 px, with no console error, no failed request, every control named and nothing wider than the screen

acceptance.given: the text roles answered by a coding agent a person already has (rihmasto models use claude-code), and a project
acceptance.when: an agent asks Rihma in the project's agent channel and a person asks goal help with a model
acceptance.then: both go through the same guard as every model call and the harness answers them; each run is one model_run in the project's ledger with the harness and its task (channel, goal), never a second one and never in the factory's; Insights' usage counts them and shows the harness as the runner; and when no model Rihmasto talks with answers but a coding agent is on this machine, a goal plan offers "Use the coding agent you already have"

requirements.statement: Every project is offered the whole of Rihmasto and every change is doable by a click and in Ask Rihma: a project's shape and state are scanned for suggested automations, each with a one-line reason, set up with one signed click or dismissed (remembered); an automation is drafted from a description (rules in English and Finnish without a model, a model checked against the allow-list for the rest) with its summary and a dry run before a person sets it up; a Set up this project checklist shows each feature that applies with its state and one click; a project is archived (hidden, read-only, restorable) and an archived one removed after a confirmation naming it, its records exported first; and a parity test keeps every cockpit control, assistant action and signed command with its other half.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24): "for automations you should be able to scan a project for suggestions of them, also define by event, and ask an agent to generate an automation based on your description." "For all projects I want to see them populated with the entire features of Rihmasto, and make sure that when you know how it happens I can also do it on a UIX level or by agent request on chat." And: "Delete so many duplicate projects." kernel/automation_suggest.py, kernel/automation_compose.py, kernel/project_setup.py, kernel/project_archive.py, kernel/setup_chat.py, kernel/assistant_ops.py (Ask Rihma's act proposals), kernel/parity.py (the tables tests/test_parity.py reads), kernel/setup_cli.py, cockpit/setup_routes.py, cockpit/static/setup.js; hooks in kernel/store.py (an archived project is hidden and read-only), kernel/copilot.py, kernel/assistant_rules.py and cockpit/server.py. docs/guides/automations.md and docs/guides/project-setup.md. No test calls a real model.

acceptance.given: projects of different shapes: an attached repository with a stated test command and enabled checks, a confidential one, one with a release in production, an ML pipeline, and a project made from an idea
acceptance.when: each is scanned for automations
acceptance.then: each gets the suggestions its shape asks for, each with a one-line reason and a draft that passes the automations' own checks (a nightly gate and tests on new commits for the repository, a failed-check notice, an alert if a role would leave the local model, a production probe every 5 minutes, a weekly evaluation, a first-build notice), notifying a relay channel when one is set up and logging a signal when none is; and scanning writes nothing

acceptance.given: a project's suggestions
acceptance.when: a person sets one up and dismisses another, in the cockpit, on the command line or by confirming Ask Rihma's proposal
acceptance.then: the set-up one is an automation in their name, signed and recorded (automation_set, automation_suggestion_accepted) and shows as set up; the dismissed one is recorded (automation_suggestion_dismissed) and not offered again; a non-person is refused and nothing changes

acceptance.given: a description in English or Finnish, such as "every night run the tests and tell me on Teams if they fail" or "öisin aja testit ja ilmoita Teamsiin jos ne epäonnistuvat"
acceptance.when: it is described without a model
acceptance.then: the rules give a draft automation (trigger, guard, action, scope, limits, and a notice to the Teams subscription when it fails), its plain-language summary and a dry run (the projects it reaches, what one firing would do, when it would first run), recording nothing; words the rules cannot read are said plainly and nothing is drafted

acceptance.given: a description the rules cannot read, and a scripted model
acceptance.when: it is described with the model

acceptance.then: the answer holds the checklist, the suggestions, the draft or the duplicates, and each change as a proposal (act) whose request is filled from the kernel's table of operations, checked before it is shown; confirming it runs that request signed by the person, and a proposal the rules would refuse (another persona, an archived project) is not offered

acceptance.given: the cockpit's map, the assistant's actions and the command line

acceptance.then: every control that changes something has an Ask Rihma action, operation, walkthrough, goal step, chat answer or a recorded reason; every control is accounted for; every assistant action and operation has a control on the map and every operation's request is a cockpit route; every signed command has its cockpit route or a recorded reason; anything added without its other half fails

acceptance.given: the cockpit in headless Chrome, dark and light, at 1440 and 390 pixels wide
acceptance.when: a person opens a project's Set up checklist and does an item, sets up a suggested automation, describes one and sets it up, archives a project, finds it in Projects, Archived, restores it, archives and removes it

requirements.statement: Rihmasto shows, for each project, every destination its capability goes to, read from what exists: the environments of its delivery plan on their paved roads (what release runs where, its URL, its health from probes and checks), the data systems and integrations it reads or writes, the channels it is used through (website chats, the relay's Teams, Slack, email and webhook subscriptions, its MCP, HTTP and OpenAI faces and who served them) and where it is published (registries and outputs), each with its environment, its state (planned, configured, delivered, healthy, failing or not measured), its last delivery and what a person can do there. A release's container image is published with the docker CLI to a registry IT names, with credentials by name only, test first and production only through IT's deploy gate; an MCP registry entry is written as a file a person submits. A destination that becomes failing feeds Health, the Review, the agent channel and the life-cycle automations.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24): "Rihmasto is the middle layer of development and all backend work and any external platform / channel or similar where the solutions are pushed and published or taken to testing." The owner agreed to a Destinations view (D-0023). kernel/destinations.py and kernel/destinations_more.py (the model), kernel/registries.py and kernel/publish.py (publishing), kernel/destinations_feedback.py and kernel/checks/destinations.py (feedback), kernel/destinations_cli.py (the command line, Ask Rihma, Deliver and Promote), cockpit/destination_routes.py, cockpit/static/destinations.js, docs/guides/destinations.md. Every registry and cloud in the tests is a fake on PATH (docker, gcloud); nothing is pushed to a real registry.

acceptance.given: a project with staging on a local-process road and production on a gcp-cloudrun road, a declared data integration, a website chat, a relay subscription and a release whose runtime declaration offers an MCP face
acceptance.when: its destinations are read (rihmasto destinations, the Destinations view)
acceptance.then: every one is listed in its group (deployed, data, channels, published) with its environment, its state, its last delivery, its health and its actions; a destination that is not ready is planned and says exactly what is missing (a road's gcloud not on PATH, an integration's binding not approved by IT, a relay variable not set, a registry's login variables not set); a relay channel whose last delivery failed is failing; reading writes nothing

acceptance.given: registries IT named in registries.json, a test and a production container registry and an MCP registry listing, and a fake docker on PATH
acceptance.when: a person publishes a release
acceptance.then: a registry that is missing or not ready refuses with exactly what is missing, recorded with who asked, and docker is never asked; a release goes to production only after it was published to a test registry, and only after IT approves the deploy_gate card the first production publish opens, IT's refusal stopping it; the token reaches docker login on its input only, never an argument, a record or an answer; the registry's digest is recorded; a failed push is recorded and the registry's destination is failing; an MCP registry entry is a server manifest file naming the published image, written for a person to submit and never submitted

acceptance.given: a project whose production stops answering its probe
acceptance.when: a feedback round runs (Check now, rihmasto destinations --check, or the destinations check)
acceptance.then: the destination becomes failing once: an incident card opens, a system post in the project's agent channel names it with the card, destination_failing is in the ledger, the Review lists it under what went wrong, an automation's event trigger destination_failing matches it, and the destinations check in Health fails; a later round that finds it healthy records destination_recovered; a round is signed by a person

acceptance.given: the cockpit in a browser, dark and light, 1440 and 390 px wide, and Ask Rihma
acceptance.when: a person follows Where this goes from the overview to Destinations, checks the destinations and publishes, and asks "where is this running?"
acceptance.then: the map shows its four groups with a state word and icon on every card and no console error, CSP violation, unnamed control or overflow; the round's and the publish's results are said; Ask Rihma answers from the destinations with Take me there and proposes opening Destinations to deliver or publish, doing nothing itself

acceptance.given: the command line
acceptance.when: rihmasto destinations <pid> [--json] [--check] and rihmasto publish <pid> --to <registry> [--release N] run
acceptance.then: destinations prints the grouped map (or JSON), and --check runs a signed feedback round; publish publishes as the cockpit does, and a refusal is a message on stderr with exit 2

requirements.statement: A person can look at and filter each project, and every project at once, as a knowledge graph of its records as the ontology links them: requirements, criteria, tests, tasks, questions, assumptions, decisions and cards, changes, releases, agent runs and models, with each node's kind, label, state, time and record, filtered by kind, relation, state, time window and words, focused on one node within a number of links, with the issues found highlighted (requirements no test checks, tests without a requirement, decisions overturned, requirements resting on a refuted assumption, broken links) and an honest note of how many more are not shown when a slice is large. The view is drawn by hand with pan, zoom and keyboard navigation, has an accessible table twin that is the default on a phone, can be saved as named views per person, opened in a chosen mode, pinned to Home and reset, is reached from Ask Rihma with its filters in the route, and from the command line; it never shows holdout content or a credential and respects who may see what.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24): "Looking at and filtering each project in an ontology / knowledge graph view would be insightful." Also: customizability must apply in every view, and every view must be usable on a phone. kernel/graph_view.py (the read model and its filters), kernel/graph_view_nodes.py (nodes, states, issues, routes), kernel/graph_view_cli.py (`rihmasto graph view`, hooked in kernel/graph_ask.py), kernel/graph_assist.py (Ask Rihma, hooked in kernel/copilot.py), cockpit/graph_routes.py, cockpit/static/graph.js, graph_draw.js, graph_panel.js, graph.css, cockpit/ui_map.json and kernel/assistant_rules.py (CONTROL_PAGES, a filter query on the graph's routes), docs/guides/knowledge-graph.md.

acceptance.given: a project whose records hold every kind the ontology defines, read through the graph's own build (kernel/graph_build.py)
acceptance.when: its knowledge graph view is read
acceptance.then: every node of the graph is in it once with its kind, family, short id, label, state (open, closed or superseded, or none for a kind with no lifecycle), ledger sequence number and time, the record that holds it and the cockpit route that opens it, every edge with its relation, origin and whether a model proposed it; and the issues are found where they are: a requirement in force no test checks, a criterion no test names, a test that checks no criterion, a decision a change overturned, a requirement resting on a refuted assumption

acceptance.given: the same project
acceptance.when: the view is filtered by kinds, relations, states, a time window, words, only issues, or focused on a node within one to four links
acceptance.then: only the nodes that pass every filter are shown (a kind with no lifecycle passes any state, a node with no time of its own passes any window), focus keeps the node and what lies within that many links in either direction, an unknown kind, relation, state, window or an out-of-range number is refused, a focus that names no node says so, and the filters round-trip through a route's query

acceptance.given: a graph of 20,000 nodes and 40,000 links
acceptance.when: its view is read with the default limit and with a focus
acceptance.then: it answers within a few seconds with at most the limit's nodes, the focus first, then the nodes with issues, then the kinds of the trace, and a note that says how many more are not shown, by kind

acceptance.given: a project with holdout scenarios carrying sentinel strings, a requirement whose text looks like a credential, an audience that may not see every kind, and access enforced
acceptance.when: the view is read for a project and across projects
acceptance.then: no sentinel appears and no graph view module names the holdout custody, the credential-looking label is replaced by a note, an audience sees only the kinds the ontology lets it, and with access enforced a project's graph is refused to an identity holding no persona on it and the view across projects leaves that project out

acceptance.given: a named person in the cockpit
acceptance.when: they save graph views for a project, choose the mode it opens in and a view it opens with, pin a slice to Home, and reset
acceptance.then: the views are kept for that person only, outside every project's ledger, each one checked as a filter the read model takes; a non-person is refused and nothing is written; Reset to default goes back to no views and the automatic mode (the table on a phone, the graph elsewhere); a pinned slice is a Home widget that reads its own slice

acceptance.given: a project
acceptance.when: rihmasto graph view <pid> runs with --kinds, --states, --focus and --hops, with --json, and with --all
acceptance.then: it prints the same read model as the cockpit (the nodes and links as two lists, the issues, how many more are not shown, or the JSON), across projects with --all, writes nothing, and refuses an unknown filter with exit 2

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma, with no model
acceptance.when: a person asks "show me how requirements trace to tests" in one or two named projects, or asks it to explain a node in the knowledge graph
acceptance.then: the answer says what the slice holds and Take me there opens the Knowledge graph with those filters in the route (one project's tab, or the page across projects with just those), or explains the node, its state, its links and its issues with Take me there focused on it; the cockpit map has the Knowledge graph and its controls (graph filters, graph or table, focus, saved views, pin) with the pages they are on

acceptance.given: the cockpit in a real browser
acceptance.when: a person opens the Knowledge graph, filters it, focuses on a node, opens its details, switches to the table, moves with the keyboard and saves, opens and resets a view, in dark and light at 1440 and 390 pixels
acceptance.then: the graph renders and each step changes what it shows, the table is the default on a phone with the filters in a sheet, nothing scrolls sideways, every control has a name, the marks' colours pass the dataviz validator against the surface they are drawn on, and there is no console error, failed request or Content-Security-Policy violation

requirements.statement: The data and context layer is visible and economical: for each project a person can see what Rihmasto knows and where it came from (sources, records, ledger, graph, spec and contract, usage, freshness, what is kept on disk), and what each Rihma agent role and surface is given right now as a context pack (each part with its source, size and estimated tokens, what was compressed and what was left out and why); a compression audit measures every pack, MCP answer and command output against the prompt economy's budgets and proposes compressions; the factory's Data view shows its stores, ledger integrity, retention and a signed clean-up; and Ask Rihma explains what an agent sees.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24): "I'm wondering how the data and context layer and everything is working, because I don't think there is much visibility to that at this moment." And: "make sure you have audited ... all the skills, tool calls ... that they are compressed, accessible." D-0024 item 2. kernel/context_parts.py, kernel/context_packs.py, kernel/context_surfaces.py, kernel/context_map.py, kernel/context_audit.py, kernel/context_chat.py, kernel/context_cli.py, kernel/data_stores.py, cockpit/context_routes.py, cockpit/static/context.js, docs/guides/context-and-data.md. Compressed: Ask Rihma's catalogue, MCP answers, and the spec, holdout, verifier and goal prompts' order.

acceptance.given: a planned project
acceptance.when: its context map is read
acceptance.then: it names each source (the request, the material map, the repository, the AI-tool conventions, the alignment) with what it holds and when it was last updated, the canon's records, the ledger's size and a verified hash chain, the graph's nodes, edges and contradictions, the spec and contract with superseded versions, model runs per role, what is kept on disk by store, and flags a record written before something it rests on changed (the spec after a settled assumption) as stale, with why; reading it writes nothing

acceptance.given: a project at each stage, and a scripted model, cell, verifier and MCP call capturing what the code sends
acceptance.when: the context pack of the intake panel, the spec, the holdout author, the builder, the verifier, Ask Rihma, goal help, an agent channel answer, the hand-off brief and the MCP tools is built
acceptance.then: each is exactly the prompt the real code path sends next (the intake panel's when intake runs again), its parts join back to it, each part names its source, stability, characters and estimated tokens with the lane's system prompt beside it; a pack that cannot be built yet says why

acceptance.given: a holdout scenario with a marked value, a secret in the environment, another project's card and a decision with a reason
acceptance.when: every pack is built
acceptance.then: none carries the holdout content, the secret's value, the other project's card or the decision's reason, every pack lists what it leaves out and why, the holdout author's content is shown only to compliance and IT, and anything of the holdout custody is replaced wherever content is shown

acceptance.given: every pack and every MCP answer and command output of a factory
acceptance.when: the compression audit runs
acceptance.then: it flags packs over their role's budget, lines said twice, a part that changes placed before parts that do not, oversized outputs and conventions sent to a role that does not need them, each with a proposed compression; the Context health per role gives average and largest pack, over-budget count and cache-friendly prefix ratios; the fixes hold: Ask Rihma's catalogue names controls by id and label with the matched entries in full (less than half its earlier size), MCP answers are compact JSON with the hand-off brief said once, the spec, holdout, verifier and goal prompts put shared instructions first, and goal help fits its rule-based steps by whole steps

acceptance.given: a factory home with projects, job logs, a snapshot no project names and a tampered ledger
acceptance.when: the Data view is read and a clean-up is proposed and applied
acceptance.then: every store is named with its bytes and files (the holdout custody by size only), every ledger's chain is verified and a broken one named, retention is stated per store, only job logs and unreferenced snapshots older than the retention are proposed, a proposal is signed by a named person as IT or operations and recorded in Rihma's own ledger, and applying it removes only items unchanged since, keeps the rest with why, and records what was removed; ledgers, records and the custody are never proposed

acceptance.given: the command line
acceptance.when: rihmasto context map|packs|pack|audit and rihmasto data, data cleanup and data apply run
acceptance.then: each prints JSON from the same kernel functions; a pack's content follows --persona; the clean-up commands are signed and refused for a persona other than IT or operations

acceptance.given: the cockpit and Ask Rihma
acceptance.when: a person reads the context map, a pack, the Context health and the Data view, proposes and applies a clean-up, and asks "what does the verifier get for T-001?" or "why didn't Rihma know about X?"
acceptance.then: the reads answer and write nothing, a pack's content follows the persona, the clean-up writes are signed and recorded; Ask Rihma answers from the pack (size against budget, largest parts, what was compressed and left out) or from where the words are (in a pack, in the records only, or nowhere), with Take me there to the Context view, and the map and Ask Rihma name both views and their controls

acceptance.given: headless Chrome
acceptance.when: a person opens a project's Context view and a pack, and the Data and context page, proposes and applies a clean-up, dark and light at 1440 and 390 pixels
acceptance.then: every pack and the map render, a pack's parts open, the holdout author's content is withheld from a developer and shown to compliance, nothing scrolls sideways, every control has a name, and no console error, failed request or CSP violation happens

requirements.statement: Live progress for long jobs. Every long job (an assessment, an adoption, a folder scan, and gate rounds, deliveries and Gnomon audits through the same adapter) shows the same live progress view: its plan (groups of steps with labels, and the model that answers a model's step), each step as it starts, ends with its counts (passed, findings, not measured, proposed), fails (why) or is skipped (why), the findings so far by area, the time it has taken and an estimate from the earlier runs of the same kind on the same project (or, honestly, none on a first run), the step running now in words, and Cancel between two steps that records nothing; read from a route with only what changed since a cursor, shown in the job's view, on the Overview and in Ask Rihma, which answers how the job is going from the progress.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): "'Assessing' should show some nice visualization of progress in different areas, since it seems to take minutes." Generalised (a concrete case shows a platform gap): one protocol and one view for every long job. kernel/progress.py (the reporter, its history and the registry), kernel/progress_estimate.py, kernel/assess_progress.py (an assessment's plan and words), kernel/progress_jobs.py (adoption, folder scan and any job that prints its steps), kernel/progress_chat.py (Ask Rihma), cockpit/progress_routes.py, cockpit/static/progress.js and progress.css; hooks in kernel/assess.py, kernel/assess_panel.py, cockpit/server.py, cockpit/source_routes.py, cockpit/walkthrough_routes.py and the views. docs/guides/assessment.md.

acceptance.given: a fixture repository and a scripted panel model
acceptance.when: the repository is assessed with a progress reporter
acceptance.then: the plan has the groups Reading the code (the revision, the inventory), Rule checks (one step per area the rules cover and the security scan), The panel (one step per perspective with the model named) and The record; every step starts in the plan's order and ends done with its verdict counts, a perspective whose model gives no answer is failed with why, the findings so far by area are the record's findings and proposals, and the record is the same as an assessment's without progress; without a model there is no panel group

acceptance.given: earlier runs of the same kind on the same project, timed
acceptance.when: a new run reads its estimate
acceptance.then: each step's expected time is the median of the last five runs, the time left counts the steps not yet ended less what a running step took (steps that run at once by the longest), a step never timed is counted as unknown and said, a step well past its usual time is said to take longer, and a first run says it has no estimate

acceptance.given: an assessment running in the cockpit
acceptance.when: a person cancels it (signed)
acceptance.then: it stops after the step that runs now, ends cancelled, records no assessment, and the cancel is noted in the project's ledger; a cancel signed by a non-person is refused and one with nothing running says so

acceptance.given: an assessment asked for in the cockpit
acceptance.when: its progress route is read with a cursor
acceptance.then: the route answers with only the events after the cursor and the job's state now, the whole plan and every step from cursor 0 (or a cursor it cannot read), the assessment view carries the latest progress, and the finished run's step times are kept for the next run's estimate

acceptance.given: an adoption that prints its step lines, a folder scan that counts files, and any job that prints its steps
acceptance.when: their progress is read
acceptance.then: each maps onto its plan: a line starts its step and ends the one before, a step passed by is skipped, the job's end ends its last step done or failed and skips what it never reached; the scan's counters fill looking through the folder, opening what matters and the map; the Jobs view, an adoption's walkthrough and a scan carry the view as live, and say they have no estimate

acceptance.given: an assessment running, and later ended
acceptance.when: a person asks Ask Rihma how the assessment is going (in English or Finnish)
acceptance.then: Rihma answers from the progress without a model: the steps done of all and the groups done, what runs now, the findings so far by area and the estimate, with the progress itself and Take me there to the Assessment tab; with none running it says so, after it ended it says how; a request to act is not taken for a question

acceptance.given: a slowed scripted assessment with the panel, in headless Chrome
acceptance.when: a person starts it from the Assessment tab and watches it
acceptance.then: the progress view shows at once, the tiles fill area by area with their findings, the panel's perspectives run with the model named, pressing an area lists its findings so far, the Overview and Ask Rihma show the same tiles, and the end hands over to the result; at 1440 and 390 px, dark and light, with no console error or CSP violation, every control named, nothing scrolling sideways, and the marks' colours passing the dataviz validator

requirements.statement: Choose a folder or file by browsing: every field of the cockpit that takes a path on the cockpit's machine (New project's existing project and a folder as the need, Add material, Shape it in chat's attach, Settings > Folders the cockpit may read, an automation's rescan folder, a Google Cloud road's workload identity file, and a walkthrough's folder step) offers Browse... (the computer's own folder dialog, when the browser runs on the cockpit's machine of a single operator) and Browse here (a folder browser in the page, from any computer or phone): places to start from, a breadcrumb, folders with git and project badges and whether the cockpit may read each, a filter and the keyboard. Browsing reads under the same rules as every read (kernel/source_guard.py), never through a link out of the allowed folders, never a system folder or a folder of keys, and records nothing; what is chosen is checked again before any use. Typing or pasting a path still works, and Ask Rihma proposes the same flow.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): "choosing an existing project should of course open a file explorer to choose it." Generalised to every local-path field, and to using the cockpit from another computer or a phone (the folder browser) as well as at the cockpit's machine (the computer's own dialog, in a child process: tkinter on Windows, osascript on macOS, zenity or kdialog on Linux). kernel/pick.py, kernel/pick_native.py, cockpit/pick_routes.py, cockpit/static/picker.js and picker.css, kernel/walkthrough_intent.py, docs/guides/inputs.md (Choose a folder or a file), docs/cockpit.md. RIHMA_PICK_COMMAND stands in for the dialog in tests, so no test opens a real one.

acceptance.given: a person in the cockpit, with folders chosen before, configured roots and allowed folders
acceptance.when: they open the folder browser (GET /api/pick/places)
acceptance.then: it starts from the folders this person chose before (kept per person in the home, outside every ledger, and only folders the cockpit may read), the roots in RIHMASTO_SOURCE_ROOTS and those allowed in Settings, the home folder and the drives that exist, each once, each saying whether the cockpit may read it and why not

acceptance.given: a folder of folders: repositories, one a project here already, dot and tool folders, a link out of the allowed folders, a folder of keys, and a folder outside the allowed ones
acceptance.when: it is listed (GET /api/pick/list)
acceptance.then: its subfolders are sorted by name, each with whether it is a git repository, the project that holds it (adopted or attached), when it changed and whether the cockpit may read it; dot folders, node_modules, .venv and the like are folded; a long folder says how many more, and the filter (q) is searched in the whole folder before the cap, so it finds those too; files only when asked and only where the cockpit may read; a link that leads out of the allowed folders is shown as not followed and its target is never read; a system folder or a folder of keys is never listed; outside the allowed folders a single operator sees subfolder names only, with Allow this folder through the signed allow route, and under enforced access it is refused; a persona that may not read a folder is refused

acceptance.given: a single operator at the cockpit's machine, and the same cockpit reached from another computer
acceptance.when: Browse... asks for the computer's own dialog (POST /api/pick/native)
acceptance.then: from the loopback browser it opens the dialog in a child process (one at a time, at most ten minutes, never holding the write lock) and answers the chosen path with whether the cockpit may read it, or cancelled; through a public origin, a proxy or under enforced access it answers 409 "use the folder browser"; where no dialog can open, 501; it records nothing. A page reached through an SSH tunnel looks like the loopback page, so while the dialog is open the page names the computer it opened on and offers Browse here instead, which closes that dialog (POST /api/pick/native/cancel, signed, from anywhere) and frees the one-dialog slot at once

acceptance.given: every field that takes a path on the cockpit's machine, and Ask Rihma
acceptance.when: a person browses for a path, or asks "adopt the project in C:\dev\x" or "open the folder picker"
acceptance.then: each field offers Browse... and Browse here beside the typed path (a field that takes a file or a folder offers File... and Folder... for the computer's own dialog), a dropped folder fills its name and says to browse for the full path, and Ask Rihma offers Plug in an existing project, started from the folder the words name (a quoted path whole, spaces and all); the map (cockpit/ui_map.json) names Browse... and Browse here

acceptance.given: New project in a browser at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark
acceptance.when: a person picks An existing project, Browse here, walks the places and the breadcrumb, filters, and chooses a folder
acceptance.then: the folder fills the field and its scan starts at once; the browser is a dialog at 1440 px and a full-screen sheet at 390 px, works with the keyboard (opening or leaving a folder keeps the focus in the list, and after choosing the focus is back on the field), scrolls nothing sideways, and the page has no console error, failed request or CSP violation

requirements.statement: The cockpit says at every moment what it is about and asks plainly: a scope bar names all projects or the one project (whose accent the whole frame then takes), one navigation (the sidebar is the project's inside a project, never a second copy of its views), a project's views grouped into five capsules (Now, Build, Run, Govern, Agents) that views join by registering and that open per persona, Inbox cards that lead with one plain Decide line and offer their choices with a meaning each, the reason only after a choice and commenting apart, a Delivery square that explains itself and switches between all projects and one, Ask Rihma that says what it talks about and answers how-to questions with steps for this project with every known value filled in, Customize on every view and on a capsule's tabs, words that fit each persona, and every view usable on a phone, with one word per concept from a glossary, and each person's view layouts kept on the server so they follow the person to another computer.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24/25): "Inbox is very unclear, it's not clear where it's asking for comments." "When you choose a project and switch views it's not clear when you view a single project and when not; transitions are not clear and which views are about what project." "When I talk to the assistant it's not clear whether it comments on the entire platform, where I'm right now, or a specific project." "I see the UIX customization button only on Home; it should work across any view." "Delivery Square view is unclear: how are you even supposed to view it? By project? On the whole platform level?" "There are now many tabs ... capsule these features so there wouldn't be so many tabs ... the user can filter them." "I didn't think necessarily to remove the idea of tabs, but there seemed to be too many of them." "Review that for each persona in each view the terms are not AI slop: they make sense in the context ... if you're a business persona the terms are like that; if you are a developer you want to understand where we are on a technical level." "Review the mobile usability of every view and feature." Ask Rihma's how-to answers were impractical ("via `rihmasto ide <pid>`", "the snapshot does not show ..."). D-0024 points 3 and 5. cockpit/static/scope.js, capsules.js (the registry: registerView), decide.js, square.js, askscope.js, viewcustom.js, words.js, shell.css; kernel/card_words.py (the plain line), kernel/assistant_howto.py (steps, filled commands, the named project).

acceptance.given: a person in the cockpit
acceptance.when: they move between Home, a project and its views, and switch project
acceptance.then: a scope bar at the top says "All projects" or "Project: <title>" with a switcher (recent projects first, "← All projects"); inside a project the frame takes the project's accent, the sidebar shows the project's name with "← All projects" and no copy of its views, the pages that exist per project too say "· all projects", and every page title states its scope; a project's views are five capsules (Now, Build, Run, Govern, Agents), each opening its own short row, with no horizontal tab row and no "Show all views"; a business owner opens a project in Now, a developer in Build, IT and operations in Run, compliance in Govern; a capsule counts what waits there; #/p/<pid>/<view> links open the right capsule; and a view registered by id (registerView) appears in its capsule, one not registered does not

acceptance.given: a card waiting on the person in a project's Inbox or the Inbox across projects
acceptance.when: they read and decide it
acceptance.then: the card leads with one plain line "Decide: <what in plain words>: <its choices>" (an escalation names the task by its title and how many times its checks failed), its choices each carry a one-line meaning and none is chosen for them, "Why? (optional, saved with your decision)" appears only after a choice, with Confirm, and the decision is recorded with or without the reason; "Add a comment" is separate and decides nothing; ids, refs and the record's own wording are under Details; a question shows "Rihma suggests: X" and pre-selects nothing; and the Inbox across projects groups the cards by project by default, by kind or age on request

acceptance.given: the Delivery square
acceptance.when: a person opens it and switches its scope
acceptance.then: it says in one line that it shows how needs move from arriving to production, across all projects; its five lanes (needs arrive, concepts to validate, being built, end users test, in production) show their counts, each a link to its items, and an empty lane says what would appear there; and its scope switch shows one project's square (its signals, its place in the pipeline, its feedback and production) or all projects

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma open on any page
acceptance.when: a person asks a question, switches what it talks about, or names another project
acceptance.then: a scope line at the top of the chat says "Talking about: <project> · <view>" or "all projects", follows the page and switches between this view, this project and the whole platform; each answer says what it was about; a question that names another project by its title is answered about that project, and Rihma says it switched; a proposal names its target; and the conversation is kept per project and one for the whole platform

acceptance.given: a project and a person with a name and persona
acceptance.when: they ask Ask Rihma how to do something (export the evidence, decide a card, report a change, run a command, build the pack, start the autopilot, work from an IDE)
acceptance.then: the answer gives numbered steps for this project: where to go as the path they click (project, capsule, view) with Take me there, what to press, and the command with the project's id, their name and persona filled in, each with a Copy button; it never shows "<pid>", "<your name>" or any other placeholder (a command whose value is not known is left out, and a missing name is asked for), and "the snapshot does not show" becomes where to look instead

acceptance.given: any page other than Home, and a project's capsule tabs
acceptance.when: a person presses Customize in the header
acceptance.then: each section of the view can be shown or hidden, moved up or down and made compact or wide, kept per person and view with Reset; in a project a tab can be hidden or pinned to the top row; a section or tab that holds a decision waiting on the person is never hidden; a hidden section leaves a note; and Ask Rihma makes the same change from words ("hide the brief", "show all sections") as a preview with Keep or Undo

acceptance.given: every top-level page and every capsule, in dark and light, at 1440 and 390 px
acceptance.when: a person opens it, as a business owner or a developer
acceptance.then: there is no console error, no failed request and no sideways scroll; on a phone the five capsules fit one row, a capsule's views scroll as chips, a project's header is compact outside its Overview, dialogs are sheets, tables are stacked rows and touch targets are at least 40 px; and labels, empty states and the Inbox's meanings are worded for the persona: plain business words for a business owner, precise technical terms for a developer, IT and operations, the same meaning in both

acceptance.given: every top-level page and every project view of a project in progress and of an adopted one
acceptance.when: a business owner and a developer each read it
acceptance.then: the interface text holds none of the filler words words.js lists (seamless, leverage, robust, it's important to note, Rihmasto has, your journey and the like) for anyone; a business owner meets no technical term from words.js's list (gate, ledger, canon, cell, round, contract, criterion, holdout, fail-first, escalation, attestation, provenance, merge, commit, MCP, triage, stale, SBOM, hash and the like) except as a glossary term whose tooltip explains it; a record's own text (titles, briefs, findings, kernel-written lines), code and ids are shown as written

acceptance.given: a concept the cockpit names (the ledger, maturity, mode, a stage, a task's status, a card's kind, a view's label)
acceptance.when: a business owner and then a developer read the same project
acceptance.then: each reads one word for it everywhere, from the glossary in words.js (a business word, a technical word and an explanation): "decision record intact" and "Decision record" for a business owner where a developer reads "ledger intact" and "Ledger", Ambition or Maturity, Done or Merged; the meaning is the same, and the stages, lanes and tab labels differ where the glossary defines both words

acceptance.given: a new project whose views have nothing in them yet
acceptance.when: a business owner or a developer opens each view
acceptance.then: every empty state says what would appear there and how it gets there (what the person or Rihma does next), in that reader's words: plain for a business owner, with the stage, command or record for a developer

acceptance.given: a person who customizes views (sections hidden, moved or resized, tabs hidden or pinned) and works on another computer
